title: Convenient and fast - allows single purchases from multiple funding sources
text: For the way I purchase this gift card reload feature is a major convenience. I have multiple sources of cards, and sometimes want to use two to three to make a single purchase. The ability to use a gift card comes in handy in those situations, so being able to reload meets my needs perfectly. The way I use it for multiple cards is to reload from one card, then another until I have distributed the funding sources. It literally takes seconds per reload, and when I am using three or more cards, it can all be done in a minute or two. Then when I need to make a purchase the entire amount is waiting. This is much faster and more efficient than purchasing multiple gift cards. You can also have your gift card balance automatically reloaded from a single funding source when the balance hits a low mark. I have not used that feature, but can see how convenient it would be for some folks who use gift cards the way I do.

I expected the balance to be reflected in my account within minutes, and the email I got confirming my order told me that's what would happen ("Typically your balance is updated within 5 minutes of your order.") title: Great to have--especially if you buy a lot of stuff on Amazon!
text: I actually am a huge fan of Amazon Gift Card and also of the "Balance Reload." In the last 6 months I've been making a lot more purchases on Amazon than I did before (for a variety of reasons) and there are two things that I've noticed that kind of bothered me: A.) When looking at my credit card statement it always just says the amount, and that it was purchased via Amazon, so there are a ton of entries for Amazon purchases that don't really mean anything to me. B.) it's really easy to spend a lot of money because, well. . . you can find pretty much anything on Amazon and it's too easy to buy with things like 1-click purchasing, subscribe and save, etc. Reloading a gift card balance means that I still get my rewards points for buying things on Amazon, but can also very easily set a budget for myself beforehand. Also, every-time that I buy something I'll be able to see how much I have left of that original amount. In short, if you buy a lot of things off of Amazon I would highly recommend using this feature. I still have some things that I buy through 1-click purchasing . . . but most everything else I use gift cards for.

title: Buyer Beware- Fandango is a Ripoff!
text: I am re-reviewing this product since Amazon pulled the option (which is the same item: Fandango Gift Card) that had all the negative reviews. Buyer beware! Fandango created a business to make it easier to purchase movie tickets online. The idea is good, but there are so many opportunities for things to go wrong and Fandango Customer Service is beyond terrible. The chances of getting burned by buying this product is very high. Since Fandango is a separate company than the theaters they deal with, you have to deal directly with Fandango if there are any issues with your tickets- the theaters cannot (and will not) help you. Fandango redeemed a $50 gift card we had and never issued tickets; when we called customer service, we were on hold for almost an hour (during which time the movie we were trying to see started). After having no luck on the phone, I filed an online complaint. It took several days for them to get back to me (in the meantime, I called again the next day and was able to get through after about a 20 minute wait). Fandango refused to issue a refund because their policy is that refunds need to be requested before the start of the show. I'd like to know how that is even possible if customer service reps don't answer the phone and don't respond to emails for days. They figure people redeeming gift certificates won't push the issue since it was a gift (not their money). There are hundreds of negative reviews about this company. Do some research before purchasing. Movie gift cards are nice, but I'd suggest going through the actual theater so that someone can assist if something goes wrong. Fandango just wants to steal your money.

I am the first to admit my Starbucks addiction and yes, I considered shelling out $450.00 for the steel embossed card, rationalizing I was really only spending 50.00 for the production cost because over the course of a year, I would spend $400.00 on their coffee anyway. title: Elegant (albeit generic) winter holiday gift card tin
text: Even though this gift-card-in-a-tin is designed to be a generic holiday gift, I purchased it as a birthday gift for a friend with a winter birthday because none of the Amazon birthday designs I saw appealed to me and because I liked the idea of a reusable gift card container. (I may be wrong, but I don't believe any of Amazon's birthday gift cards are packaged in tins.) The design of this one is obviously intended to be suitable for any winter holiday -- Christmas, New Year, Hanukkah (note that this snowflake has six points, like the Star of David, and is blue, the official Hanukkah color), Kwanzaa, Festivus, etc. This generic design worked in my favor because I intended to use it for a birthday gift, but if I had been shopping for a holiday gift, I would have preferred a design specific to that particular holiday. I generally avoid giving people gift cards because I find them impersonal (as well as for other practical reasons that I won't go into here), but when I do, I prefer to present them in gift containers instead of just slipping them into cards for a couple of reasons: a package make the gift card a bit less guessable and reduces the chance that the gift card will be overlooked or discarded by mistake, as can happen when it's enclosed in a card. However, I also try to be environmentally responsible and choose packaging, like this tin, that can be re-used over and over, in place of wrapping paper that is often thrown out after a single use. One selling feature for this Amazon card was that at the time I bought it, it came with free one-day shipping. I'm a Prime member, so I would have gotten "free" 2-day shipping anyway, but as a chronic procrastinator, every little bit helps. Overall, I was pleased with this gift card/gift tin and thought it looked rather classy, as far as gift card boxes go, and it's likely that I'll purchase another (or similarly packaged gift card) next year.

You’ll need to know the balance but checking the amount is extremely easy. Overall, these are great to gifts because the person you are giving it to has the option to use at multiple places. title: I use this every single day
text: I'm a Mac person but Microsoft really got me with Office 365. At first I was annoyed to have a subscription service but since I'm part of a family of 5, it worked out that we got our money's worth. Office isn't a perfect application--I LOVE Excel more than Numbers and Word is more complete than Pages but can t clunkier, not organized as well, and not as good for Desktop publishing and images. But Office at this price is excellent. The next thing I hated was that 365 switched from the number of devices to the number of users. I could STAND that my home computer that my 3 kids used had to have separate logins for applications on the same computer. BUT, when Dropbox continually refused to offer smaller monthly packages and limited the number of devices on their free version, I started to look elsewhere. Lo and behold Microsoft OneDrive was my answer. And it was ALREADY INCLUDED with my Office 365. Now everyone in my family has 1 TB of OneDrive storage and they can access it on their iphones, laptops or wherever they can get an internet connection. I can share REALLY LARGE VIDEO FILES with as many parents from the school that I want. I can share lots of school videos for the parents to download AND I don't have to store them on my computer. In other words I can have them on the cloud (OneDrive) and they don't have to sync to my computer. This frees up a lot of space on my computer. (I save copies on external drives of course.) Good-bye Dropbox! So this has become an essential part of my life and one of the subscription services I consider a must-have along with Amazon Prime.

title: Convert Your Visa Gift Cards
text: So while it sounds terrible to complain about a gift... I always hated it when people would give me those Visa or Discover gift cards. They are such a pain to manage and I've always had nothing but issues trying to use them. If you don' t have the full amount available on the card, some merchants won't let you use them. I would also be very careful about only using them for things that I knew I would never need to return... because what a nightmare that would be if you no longer had the card. Bottom line... I hate those things. But then a few months back, I had a revelation to simply use that Visa gift card to buy myself an Amazon Gift card (reload) and have it placed directly into my account. Regardless of the amount... whether it is some odd leftover like $23.78 or an even $100, you can load it to your Amazon gift card balance and dump those stupid Visa Gift cards. I know I'll definitely use the Amazon funds, and Amazons gift card balance management makes it incredibly convenient. Plus... some of those Visa and Discover gift cards lose value over time due to "maintenance fees." So if you're like me and hate dealing with those things, or throw them in a drawer and forget about them... do yourself a favor and convert them over to Amazon bucks. Life becomes so much easier!

title: No Print of Value | Cheap Nylon Packaging with Visible Serial #
text: Gift cards are simply the best option for allowing the recipient to buy what they need, taking guesswork out of planning and gifting people for occasions. Unless they have a public wishlist on Amazon or you are making a custom DIY gift for the recipient, you might very well buy a gift that isn't a useful to them, specially if you don't know their likes and dislikes. Therefore in the time when buying random physical gifts are obsolete, fancy gift cards need to be given a special place in terms of customizable presentation, designs, colors and styles - specially on a platform like Amazon. You would think that you will be spoiled with various beautiful and upend choices of gift cards packaged in great variety of styles and designs. But to my astonishments, the range of choices are very limited, often to very cheap and dollar store type thrown together packagings. Neither are environmentally friendly, using chemical heavy processes to produce gloss and sparkles. Another option is to go with a plain card design and then get a separate gift wrapping and boxing solutions. A search for that yielded few and poor selection of results. This seemed somewhat better than others but apart from the dreadful faults shown in other reviews such as the card arriving bent and with faults, no thought has been given to the process; (1) The box arrives inside an ugly, cheap nylon packaging with a sticker label that reveals ALL the serial numbers and information necessary to use the gift card without even opening it. How dumb is that. This can open the gift card to theft as you don't even have to open the box to use the code to claim the value. I wanted to open the box and inspect it to be sure all is as should be and adding a few more customized items to it. You couldn't do that because of that stupid and dumb nylon packaging. Why not open the nylon packaging then, you might ask. Since I didn't have a prior experience with this design, I didn't know if I could open the nylon package since the critical information regarding the code were on the seal line that closed the box. I imagined and hoped the information is also printed on the card but wasn't sure since there were references in reviews and other places that nothing is printed on the cards. They are just cosmetic and generic. I know this might sound a no brainer, but given how often these things are overlooked, I wanted to be sure. I opened the box and the information was on the card's back but then I still don't understand why you would print it on a nylon packaging that the unit came in; something that a user should throw away. A blank and clear nylon packaging was sufficient and would avoid creating confusion. Also rather than a nylon, I preferred an eco friendly packing option such as a cardboard paper of some sort. (2) Dumber still, the value on the card is not printed. This was a customized amount not listed among options. This is for making it easier for the supplier not having to bother with an additional step of printing something. Nevertheless, that sometimes matter and important to the giver and receiver. Most cards you buy from the shelves also do not have a value printed unless you buy the pre-loaded ones at set values. The point of getting a customized card is to have it customized. text: These cards are one of the best options to use for holiday gifts to people in the service industries around your kids’ education systems - bus drivers, matrons, aids to teachers, ancillary teach staff, school security guards, the list goes on. Giving cash somehow seems crass - culturally I am not used to just paying in cash as appreciation for someone’s work through the semester when it comes to near the holidays. Giving gifts is a hit or miss, mostly a miss - teachers and staff specifically mention how they are tired of receiving coffee mugs and teacher-branded cute showpieces and other general merchandise. Amazon cards are among the best options, particularly as the recipients can club them together and buy what they really want. The holiday theme, the lower denominations, and the multi-pack all go towards making the process easier.

text: I thought it would be a fun gift for my ex-college roommate. We share the same taste in music. NOT, NOT, NOT. If you buy it from the US and send the PIN overseas they won't honor it. Amazon says nothing about it, but when you get the card and your friend enters the PIN Spotify will not accept it. Then you read the fine print on the card and there it is... only you have to buy the card to get that part of the fine print. Even worse - I can't use the card for my own account because I have a family plan. This has been a two day dumpster fire so far. I gave it 3 stars because the one star reviews seem to be written by bots most of the time. But really... it's a zero star deal if you want to give a gift to an overseas friend. Note: I love Spotify itself which is why I wanted to share it. I cannot understand why they make it so hard to give as a gift. I didn't want to go to Amazon or Target to buy it. I wanted to give my money to Spotify itself, but they are strangely obtuse about this simple thing. [EDIT - When I contacted them Amazon called me back immediately and agreed with me that the posted information was misleading. In spite of the "no refunds" warning they reimbursed me that same day. Excellent customer service.]

title: Beware if purchasing multiple values.
text: I would attach a photo, but I’d have to blur out the gift card number, so just look at the photo on Amazon. If you are purchasing multiple gift cards with different values, there is nothing on gifting options to complete the specific card for individual recipients. So, if you choose to complete the gifting options and the person uses their receipt to return the card for some reason, it may or may not use the correct card. Same problem when you received them. You may Ave a back with $1000 worth of gift cards and no indicator of the value of the individual cards. You can find it out if you go to your order online, since it will list the serial numbers of the cards. So, you’ll have to do some detective work, but then there is no place on the gift card holder to write the value, who it’s to and who it’s from. The cards are plain white, so you could write on it with a marker, but not the best. I ordered about a dozen of different values and was very disappointed and dissatisfied. So, word of advice. Pick a different one from Amazon that has the value, or you can place the value somewhere. Order different values separately and wait a day between orders. That costs Amazon a little more for shipping, which I’m not a fan of, but it might encourage them to think more about their customers. After all - this is Amazon and not the discount brand.

title: Easy, convenient, and a great way to budget your purchases!
text: I love Amazon! I tend to always look here first before I purchase anything. Not just because Amazon has just about anything, but they have all the colors and the options that I could ever possibly want, including ones that I didn't even know I wanted until I saw them. In addition, I love being able to read through the customer reviews. I have been swayed away from items that I thought I wanted because of the reviews, and have instead purchased a similar item based on good reviews. I have had very good experiences by following those guidelines. I never have to fear when ordering through Amazon. As a prime member, I know when my items will arrive, I know that they will arrive on time, I know that they will be packaged well, and based on my reading through reviews? I pretty much know that I will enjoy the item that I receive. There are so many reasons to purchase an Amazon gift card and to keep the balance loaded. It is so much easier to budget for your purchases, transfer gift card balances, or simply keep track of your Amazon spending. In addition, they almost always have specials that they run if you load a certain amount. Since I frequently make purchases (including monthly subscriptions), this is the best way to keep my statements from being cluttered with several small Amazon purchases each week. Instead, there is a withdrawal for the gift card purchase, and then all the smaller purchases just come out of that. Amazon also makes it so easy to do!

title: Yes, the card is really loaded despite what the packaging says
text: I bought this as a gift. It comes in a sealed package which is really nice. However, here is a word of advice: on the package itself, it states that the card is not valid until activated by a cashier. This had me a bit worried that I had just paid $50 for an unloaded gift card. I opened the package so that I could get the code off the back of the card and check the balance on the website provided. Thankfully, the card IS loaded with the $50. I wish I would have left it in the package it came in because it would've looked better as a gift, but I felt I had to make sure it was actually loaded first. So learn from my mistake- yes, the card is loaded. And if you really want to be sure it is loaded, it provides a website you can go to to check the card balance. However, if you're buying this as a gift and want to keep it in the packaging (looks nicer that way) then you can be rest assured that it is actually loaded and you don't have to open it to check.

title: Gift Cards Are Great - If Presented Properly
text: I ordered a gift card for each of my children and grandchildren for Hannukah. I wrote a different (although similar) note to each and signed it from my spouse (a stepparent) and me. The first card arrived today to my middle daughter. The rest are arriving tomorrow for some reason. I received a rather confused call from my granddaughter asking me if I had sent her a gift card. I asked her why the confusion as to who the card was for. She sent me a photo of the enclosures. A generic note saying that it was from me and that it was for her mother (but she thought that perhaps I addressed the card to her mom for mail purposes). My note to my daughter was left off. My granddaughter thought that we had sent her $100 and it was all confusing. Tomorrow, she will hopefully get her $75 gift card and hopefully a note. But I resent paying as much as I did only to have Amazon ignore it and send a generic card. Very disappointing. Update: Amazon lost my granddaughter’s gift card. They will replace it and made a point out of telling me that it will be at no charge to me! And, if all goes well, she will get it tomorrow, 5 days after her mother, aunts, uncle and cousins all got one. Good thing she is old enough to understand that its late arrival is no reflection on what we think of her!

title: Great idea, terrible execution by Amazon
text: I was really excited about the “anytime” gift card concept. I can keep a stack of gift cards ready for birthdays or last-minute gifts but pay for them and decide on the amount only when I need them! Unfortunately, Amazon seems to have launched this product without testing it. What a nightmare the first time I tried to load one! I eventually figured out a way to do it, so let me save you the trouble: You need to scan the QR code on the back of the gift card. As far as I can tell, Amazon hasn’t released any software that allows us to do this. You could type in the extremely long serial number manually, but the card is glued to the envelope right over the serial number, so revealing that requires you to remove the card from its gift envelope, thus ruining the gift envelope. After many internet searches and three(!) third-party apps, here’s what worked for me: Using my iPhone, I downloaded the free QR code reader named simply “Scan” from the App Store. Use that app to scan the QR code on the back of the gift card. (It’s very difficult to do because the code is so small and not centered in the window. Some apps won’t scan a code this small, but Scan has been working for me.) The app will take you to an Amazon.com page and request your user name and password. Don’t enter this now! (I doubt it’s a good idea to put your Amazon password into ANY free, third-party app...) Click the Safari icon in the lower right corner to open that page in your phone’s browser. Then log in to Amazon using your user name and password. Finally, you should be taken to a page where you can load a balance onto your gift card. Amazon will probably make you re-enter your credit card information for “security purposes,” so have your card ready. The good news is that so far, I haven’t experienced any of the problems that other reviewers mentioned where the recipient couldn’t use the card because the balance had been applied to the *purchaser’s* account! (Ugh!) I hope Amazon fixes these problems soon, because the idea is great and I’d find many reasons to use these gift cards if it were easier!

title: Love It!
text: These Amazon gift cards that come with a blank greeting card are extremely convenient! They usually arrive in 24-48 hours. I also like how many of the gift cards themselves have a design on them as well, and that you can buy them in so many different denominations. If you buy them at the store, they usually only come in the one design with the "a" on it and have only 3 or 4 limited denominations that they can be purchased in. I've bought a couple of these for birthdays, holidays, and anniversaries. Most people I know buy something or another through Amazon. Another option I like when I'm purchasing a last minute gift (like on Christmas Eve), is the option to purchase an Amazon gift card and have it emailed to you or the recipient. It isn't nearly as pretty, but it is a very convenient option with instantaneous delivery which also allows you to purchase in various different denominations. Both the greeting card and email options also save you from the hassle of running to a retail store and waiting on a long line to buy one or two gift cards during the holiday season.

title: A way to manage those pesky rebate cards we get in the mail
text: This feature is one of my favorite things on Amazon. At first I had no clue why I would purchase a gift card on Amazon in my own account. Then I got one of those "rebate gift cards" from an item I purchased and had to figure out what to do with a Visa or MC that had only $20, $30, $40 on it. I certainly didn't want to carry it around or track how much I had spent and how much was left. That is where the gift card balance reload feature on Amazon came to the rescue. I was able to register my rebate card with Amazon, purchase a gift card for the exact balance left on the card, wait for confirmation, and then toss the card, never to worry about it again. This is too easy! Overall, anything that makes life just a bit simpler or more convenient is a plus. Amazon hit the nail on the head by allowing us to use gift cards, rebate cards and more to purchase Amazon "bucks" that we can use to actually get something we want. Thank you Amazon!

title: Amazon eGift Cards are a great and convenient gift to send to anyone
text: Amazon eGift Cards are a great and convenient gift to send to anyone, especially when we can't be with them in person for a birthday or any special occasion. It's easy to purchase, it's customizable, it is sent by email, and it arrives fast (which is great for when we only remember someone's birthday at the last minute). Another great feature is that, since 2005, Amazon gift cards do NOT expire. All money/pre-paid gift cards (such as Visa, AE and others) always have an expiration date and, some of them, even start charging a monthly maintenance fee a few months before the expiration the date. For this reason, the first time I received a money/pre-paid gift card as a gift, I purchased an Amazon eGift Card for myself and, from then on, I always use money cards I receive to reload my Amazon eGift Card so I don't have to worry about expiration dates or about not losing the money card, and don't even need to keep track of my Amazon eGift card number because my Amazon eGift Card balance is always automatically available on my Amazon account every time I am check out a purchase and I don't need to enter any card number.

The first time I tried to purchase something, I caught this, and unchecked it, but then I forgot something so I backed out before finishing, went back and did more shopping, added something else to my cart, and then checked out. This second time checking out, I thought the gift card balance was unchecked, but I honestly didn't pay much attention since I had already gone through those steps (and all I did was add another product to my cart), so this second time I went much more quickly. Only after reviewing the order a day later (when I went to check on something), did I realize that Amazon had again automatically credited the entire gift card balance to the order. Not a huge deal, just a little annoying. Otherwise, everything went great, and I have had no other issues/complaints.

It has since been brought to my attention that the company now has such a high threshold for free shipping and a high shipping rate that it is now cost prohibitive to purchase from them online. Even when given a gift card! I'm now forcing friends and family to spend more just to get a gift! If you can find an actual store, maybe you're alright but mail order is out of the question. It used to be fun. People would buy special packages of steaks or burgers. Or try something out of the ordinary. Now it seems its more of a hassle to find something you'll like and not spend more then the gift cards! The weight of the meats is small, the postage is high and adding heavy potatoes to a combo isn't really "special". I will NOT continue buying these in the future.

title: Perfect way to convert used (or new) giftcards to Amazon with no fees.
text: I had a small stack of used giftcards sitting around. You know, when the balance gets to like $2.34, and you don't know what to do with them? Easy to "recharge gift balance" with all of those cards sitting around! 1. Look up the balance. 2. Click Account & Lists 3. Select Gift Cards 4. Click the yellow "Reload Your Balance" button 5. Enter Gift Card balance under the $(Other) block. 6. Click Buy Now 7. Under Payment Method, Select Change and enter gift card information. 8. Verify and click "Place Order" You can repeat with all of your applicable gift cards. Just remember to go through and clean up your payment methods when you are done, so you don't have 13 random debit cards to choose from in the future.

text: Buying gifts for certain family and friends can be a pain. It seems like every time I get them a game, or something they would like they either do not like it anymore, or they already own it. I ended up deciding to get a Bahama Breeze card instead because it is something I know they would like, that they can use, and that will make them happy. I mean who does NOT love food? This gift card was perfect for that. It came quickly, and they had no problem using it. Check out with the card was simple, and they were able to get exactly what they wanted. I am happy that Amazon provides the ability to get these cards so that I know no matter what, I am able to get something for that anyone will use and enjoy. I know that some people think that a gift card is impersonal, or not something that you put a lot of thought into, however I think that if you pick something they will love and use it is great. Plus, I was able to include a little note telling them exactly why I got it for them which made it a little more personal than just handing them cash. I will be buying gift cards again through Amazon since the process was so easy and streamlined, and since I experienced no problems with my purchase, or the recipient using the card. I would suggest buying gift cards through Amazon to my friends, and my family without a hesitation.

title: I have found lots of uses for purchasing an Amazon gift card!
text: Here are a couple benefits to buying an Amazon gift card I don't think everybody thinks of. I read it before on some article about uses for Amazon gift cards and I think they are brilliant ideas. Before I share my first one, let me start by saying that I don't remember how I lived to before Amazon and I don't want to try to remember it. It's kind of a similar feeling to when I think about how people must've lived before the Internet and how hard it must have been to have to go look things up at the library instead of googling them. So my first use for an Amazon gift card is actually just to build up a gift card amount to use to purchase my many many products that I am constantly making orders for on Amazon instead of using a credit card or debit card for each of those orders that early. The reason for that being that I ended up with line after line and page after page of Amazon orders on my credit card which made it really difficult to find any other purchases on there, most importantly possibly purchases that I did not make. My credit card has been stolen several times and the only way I found out was because I happened to see a purchase on The statement that was not familiar. Virtually impossible to do that now one almost everything says Amazon on my credit card bill. So instead I use an Amazon gift card to buy everything on Amazon and that leaves my credit card clear of Amazon plastered all over the statement. The second thing that I use it for is actually just to get rid of other odds and ends of gift cards such as other visa gift cards and things like that that you get as a gift. title: Tamper proof sealed. Gift box moved smoothly!
text: I bought this for our family's Christmas white elephant gift exchange this year. I put this with a big tub of Lysol wipes in a gift bag. It seemed fitting for 2020. I wanted to gift something that anyone could use, and an Amazon giftcard seemed like the best way to do that. My husband gifted the new Amazon Echo dot, and honestly, our gifts were the only one's that were traded! The gift card was traded the most at 4 times, so I felt good knowing that the giftcard was a good way to go this year. I think we all can use one right now. This giftcard came in a sealed plastic wrapper, so you know that it's not been tampered with. There's also a receipt that shows the giftcard amount and I recommend that this should be put with the giftcard when gifting, just in case any issues arise when they're redeeming. My dad actually ended up with the giftcard, so I will update if he has any issues. Our giftcard box came in good shape. It moved up & down smoothly and didn't have any noticeable creases anywhere in person. The one thing I wish it had was the giftcard amount listed on the giftcard itself. Aside from the receipt, there's no amount listed anywhere, so we had to write $20 on the back with a marker. Not the most presentable way, but we needed something that could be seen easily so the white elephant game could continue with ease. I seen that other reviewer's giftcards had the total on the upper corner of the giftcard itself, so that's what I was expecting. Amazon giftcards ordered online rarely have that, so I wasn't completely expecting it, but hoping this one would be different. This is one thing that would be a great addition to all Amazon giftcards. I've ordered one from almost every listing on here, and that's the one thing that's been a bit aggravating each time. I folded the receipt and stuffed it behind the black giftcard. These are not the shiny plastic giftcards. These, like almost all of the giftcards bought on here, are a thick card stock material. Most people probably don't care if they're just going to load &dispose, but I prefer the plastic ones personally, because I like to save mine up. There's really not much else to say about a giftcard. I hope my experience and pictures help give you an idea of what to expect in person. Please let me know if this helps. It gives me that little encouragement to continue to take the time to share my experiences.

title: No tamper proof! Comes sealed in plastic &envelope glued closed.

If you're purchasing this outright to gift, I hope these pictures also help give you an idea of what to expect in person. I know there are many amazon gift card options to choose from, and I've bought many, so I just wanted to show what this particular gift card looks like in person. FYI...This is the hard cardboard style giftcard, which I've noticed is what seems to come in most options. Even the one's that come in the fancier box options on here. This is shinier. Some are matte. Most people probably don't care, but just thought I'd mention it. *Tips if looking because of a bundle promo: Don't forget to add this in your cart along with the accompanying item if this is offered as a promotion. But...You must get to this page by clicking on the promotional add or it will not count. I originally tried just searching for a $10 gift card and adding it, but it would not deduct the discount when doing it that way. The link should be on the product page. Just click the words giftcard, and it should bring you here. I personally got mine as part of the Ring doorbell pro &Chime pro bundle on Cyber Monday. I actually thought it was going to be emailed for some reason, but it arrived in the box with the Chime Pro. I hope this review helps someone in some way.

title: A classy box, especially nice if you're not putting it in a card.
text: I bought two of these from my daughter's volleyball team to their coaches for our volleyball banquet. In past years they've always received some type of volleyball item, and me and the other mom's thought we'd get them $50 gift cards instead so they can buy themselves whatever they want. I chose the gift box option, because it looks very classy and comes ready to gift if you want. I personally chose to put these in a little gift bag for a little mystery, and the fact they came with boxes really made this idea work. They quality of the packaging was beautiful. The box has a beveled Amazon printed allover the entire top lid, including the sides. I do wish that the actual gift cards themselves were plastic like a credit card or how most other gift cards usually are. These are a thick stock paper/cardboard material. It still works, and for our purpose, I was happy. I would suggest getting a plastic option that doesn't come with a box if you're going to just unbox it and put this in an actual card. I almost bought these to do that, and figured at least I'd have a little gift box if needed. I now would recommend not doing that unless you are gifting in the box. I mean, you still could. It's just a gift card after all. The one meant for placing in a card will look higher quality for that purpose. But for handing someone a card with this gift box accompanying it would be a great idea, too. This came in a sealed plastic bag to protect it, and so you can tell it hasn't been tampered with. It has an instruction card, which I placed in the lid, as well as a receipt incase there's any issues, which I folded and put under the gift cards. This is my experience, and I hope this helps with your gifting ideas and needs. I hope my pictures help give you an idea of to expect in person.

title: "Guaranteed delivery"  from Amazon turned out to be a lie. They guarantee only to waste your time when you call about delays
text: This will likely be my last review ever- plan to really go out of my way to avoid buying anything from Amazon in the future. I Ordered this product on the basis of a "guaranteed next day delivery" for a friend's birthday. I took a screenshot of of webpage showing the guarantee screen. The next day, checking status, Amazon's website tracking indicates a delay of 2 extra days - 3 day delivery instead of next day. I called up Amazon expecting some kind of help on expediting the shipment, or at least giving me the option to switch it over to an electronic gift certificate. Instead, I spent an hour with different call center folks in India trying to smooth talk me into accepting that there is no option but to wait for deliver, that they could not cancel and re-issue the order. Basically they provides a series of hollow apologies but didn't lift a finger. What a load of BS... I told them that if I cancelled the order and placed a new one , my gift would get there faster than the "best that amazon support could do for me". At this point, they said they coudn't cancel the order either. I asked to speak to a supervisor and here's where I was extremely disappointed to hear exactly the same thing. When I asked them what the definition of the guarantee was, I got absolute silence... Not only that, but the supervisor seemed to be annoyed at the question itself. They would not lift a finger to help me and didn't offer anything. After pressing the supervisor on the fact that I placed my order with Amazon on the basis of guarantee and an expectation that a birthday present would arrive on birthday, she finally said the best she could do was give me one month free on my prime subscription. I realized these people were only going to delay me further. I declined and informed the supervisor that I wanted to cancel the order immediately. She at least helped me with this cancellation.... Immediately afterwards, I ordered an apple store e-gift certificate in a few seconds, problem solved. Friend happy. True, it was not in the pretty package I had planned for... but at least it made it on time. From my perspective, Amazon had previously been a great vendor, the A to Z guarantee was honored by them in several occasions, great support. But obviously things there are going downhill. So long Amazon.

title: New Amazon Gift Card reloading process: unexpected & time consuming.
text: The previous system was very clear and easy to use. Reloading one’s Gift Card was quick and the funds were available immediately. There was no announcement or explanation for this change… a change that does not appear to make things any easier or better for the Amazon customer. Now, it appears we have to purchase a gift card from ACI Gift Cards, Inc. and then this Gift Card is supposed to automatically be applied to our Amazon Gift card balance in about 5 minutes… with the caveat that it may take longer. I started maintaining a Gift Card balance because I use Virtual Credit Cards for internet purchases. Virtual Credit Cards can only be used at one merchant. Unfortunately, Amazon can charge any given item to any one of 5 (or more) different merchants with little or no information about which merchant will be charged at the time of purchase. This means that orders with multiple items could have some item purchases rejected due to payment issues. Fixing this can delay the order process for days. Reloading the Gift Card using a Virtual Credit Card is a way to get around this problem. The only real downside is having to maintain a balance with Amazon that can only be used at Amazon.

title: A gift card... what could go wrong? Here’s what did and how Amazon fixed it...
text: It’s a reloaded gift card. What could possibly go wrong? Actually, I did have something go wrong. On Black Friday, I got an offer for an extra $10 to refill a gift cart for $100. That’s 10% free... I’ll definitely take that deal. I clicked the link which took me to the checkout, and I wondered why I didn’t see the $10 bonus anywhere. I went ahead anyway and checked out. I got the $100, but not the $10. I was pretty bummed, but I had no way to prove that I’d clicked on the $10 bonus link. About a week later, I got irritated enough to actually reach out to customer service via the in-app chat. To my surprise, CS acknowledged the mistake and credited me the $10. The catch was that it’d be applied at my next purchase. Again, it was not visible to me (afaik). It was successfully applied on my next purchase, so everything worked out correctly in the end I have always trusted Amazon to do the right thing, but this time I had no evidence to prove what I’d done. The fact that they honored their offer earned deep trust from me. I’m a happy customer (again).

text: UPDATE TO THIS REVIEW: I am raising my rating from 4 stars to 5 because I have found a way to not use my gift card balance when I don't want to use it. Yay! For those of you who feel the same about this as I do, you can save your gift card balance up and make a purchase using your other payment methods. Click on the blue link in checkout to change your payment method. When you scroll all the way down the page you will find a small sentence saying to use the gift card balance for this purchase. There is a check box next to it and all you have to do is uncheck that box. You can then save your gift card balance for a different purchase you may be planning and the full price can be charged to whichever payment method you choose. I love the fact that I am able to reload my gift card balance. It's a good feature. However, it's kind of awkward to do it. And it's not instantaneous. It can take up to 15 minutes. My son wanted me to buy him a headset on Amazon. He handed me cash. I logged in to place an order for him. But I didn't want to spend my own gift card balance. But Amazon would have used that first on my purchase. I wanted to keep that on my account. So, instead of just buying his headset, I went in and loaded the amount I would need to the balance. Great. Except there was a delay. So I had to wait and reload the page. Then wait some more and reload the page again until finally the balance was available and I ordered his item. I'm no tech expert, but shouldn't there be an easier way to simply say that I don't want to use my gift card balance on a purchase?

title: Cheap looking Thick paper cards that may peel off
text: These gift cards are made of thick stock paper/cardboard. They add a tacky substance to prevent the cards from moving around. Tacky substance + paper material = peeling. They are not good gift cards to give out as they feel and look cheap, and that's assuming you can get that tacky substance off without peeling part of the gift card (some of which will actually peel off the card number). You should expect that at least 1 out of the 4 will be un-giftable because the tacky will stick so much that the surface from the gift card will peel off with the tacky substance. You are much better off getting another product where they use the standard plastic gift cards (like the ones they sell in the Starbucks stores)

text: What a great gift idea... I mean.. the idea of having gift available at all times without having to have anything specific, who comes up with these things? To put a few dollars in an envelope on a birthday or holiday is something my wife and family frown on..its in our opinion a poor approach to telling someone that you care via the gift giving continuum. So, this is a great alternative and avoid us having to go to a pharmacy or the grocery store to buy a gift card. Plus Amazon is our favorite shopping site so its exciting for us to encourage others to use the site and then we can elaborate on how much we save and how convenient it is to use. It may sound corny, but genuinely, those that purchase hundreds of things from Amazon a year, like my family does, will find that they are 'tied' to the Amazon family in a way that is unlike your standard vendor user relationship... Amazon is a new way to live in many regards. A shopping portal that says, we can send it to you whenever you want.. whatever u want we can get it for you so long as someone is selling it and ... oh yea.. get some real reviews from other people.... before you buy it. title: Holiday Gift Cards In Great Snowflake Tins, Love These!
text: UPDATE 12/7/13: If you're thinking of ordering these for the 2013 holidays don't wait until the last minute. Last year the $50 denomination was sold out by mid December and they didn't get any more until after the holidays. These are nice looking holiday gift cards with great, versatile snowflake boxes. The boxes are NOT cardboard. They are tins(metal containers) which look very nice and open and close well. They are a good quality. Although they have a snowflake design, they are attractive enough to be repurposed into things like containers to hold earrings or other small items after the holidays. When I placed my order I was a bit worried because the order said [Paper Gift Certificate], but the gift cards I received are regular plastic cards like credit cards. I bought one $50 Amazon gift card with snowflake tin that I am giving for the holidays. But I also plan on giving a lot of other types of gift cards for Xmas and most don't come with any kind of box or container which means you have to buy a little box for about $1.99 or find a card to put them in to make them presentable gifts. So I spent an additional $200 to get 4 extra snowflake tins to use for the holidays for other gift cards. I have young nieces who will just love these containers. And now that I have a $200 Amazon Gift Card Balance I'm using it to pick up other holiday gifts on Amazon. Win-Win for me as the tins are basically free since I shop a lot on Amazon. Plus I paid for it with my Amazon.com Rewards Visa so I'm pretty sure I'll earn 3 points per $1 spent.(I don't think there is any exclusion for gift cards. Should find out in a few days.) With the Free One-Day Shipping I was able to order these on Dec 9th and received them on Dec 10th. They were securely packaged stacked inside a cardboard wrap around mailer. I would have preferred them to ship in a regular box with each one individually bubble wrapped, but none of mine were damaged. Originally Amazon was only offering these gift cards in denominations of $50 (they got a bunch of low ratings because people wanted more denominations), but more choices have been added. Choose from $50, $75, $100, $150, $200, $250, $350, $500, $750 & $1000. UPDATE 12/18/12: I guess these have become quite popular, the $50 denomination is sold out.

title: DON'T BUY A GIFT CARD. THEY ARE NOT INSURED AND NUMBERS ARE EASILY STOLEN
text: My husband and I registered with Amazon for our wedding. We had people coming from all over, so it seemed like the simplest choice. Many people got us Amazon gift cards. After the wedding and honeymoon we added the Amazon gift cards to our account and to our dismay one of the $100 gift cards we had already been loaded to someone else's account. I contacted Amazon about this and they told me I needed to contact the person that purchased it for us to see if they purchased it with a credit or debit, and to have the credit or debit card company reimburse them. Our friend who purchased the card for us bought it from a store with cash. She informed the store about what was happening and the store told her there was nothing they could do. When we received the card it was new, still sealed in the cardboard sleeve, with the code on the back still covered, and yet someone was still able to steal the information and load it to their account. To top it off Amazon could see who's account it was loaded to, and yet still refused to help me. I wanted to do a little further investigating regarding the matter, so I went on to Amazon's website and pulled up all the different gift cards you can purchase from them. I scrolled down, and was shocked to see all the negative reviews on the gift cards. Apparently tons of people have faced this same issue and still Amazon has done nothing to change the situation. The lack of care on Amazon's part is insulting and disgraceful. It is a waste to purchase one of their gift cards because there is absolutely ZERO insurance. When you purchase someone a visa giftcard they're insured and if theives steal the information you can be reimbursed.

title: I normally hate gift cards, but Amazon gift cards are okay
text: When people give me gift cards, it's often a chore to use them. I forget to carry them with me, I buy something but forget there was a gift card in my wallet, they expire or start deducting fees if you don't use them right away, or in the worst case I can't find anything that I want or need from that particular store. It's also a pain trying to keep track of how much is left on each card and what you spent it on. On the flip side, sometimes when I do remember that I have a gift card, I feel almost obligated to spend the gift card on something nice instead of on my normal purchases like personal hygiene products and food--you know, because the person who gave me the gift card probably didn't envision buying me deodorant and eggs. (But then again, maybe they thought I could use some deodorant and thought giving it to me directly would be too rude.) Aside from these generalities, I have a few specific thoughts on certain types of gift cards. Restaurant gift cards: Of all the gift cards I get, restaurant gift cards are the easiest to use. Either I get to try a new restaurant that I haven't visited before, or I get treated to a meal or two at one of my favorite places. I take my wife out to dinner and use the gift card in one or two visits. If there will only be a few bucks on the gift card after our meal and tip, we usually add drinks and/or dessert. Best Buy: I hate Best Buy. Fortunately, nobody gives me Best Buy gift cards. Kmart: I don't normally go to Kmart, but at least I can go there to convert a Sears gift card into a Red Lobster gift card. Lowes: I buy a ton of stuff at Lowe's so I definitely use those gift cards, but it's disappointing to me if I end up spending the gift card on a bunch of random little supplies instead of on tools or on a larger project. Sears: I hate Sears and the closest one is more than an hour away. Target: I don't normally go to Target Walmart: Normally I just buy small, random, everyday stuff AMEX/Visa/Mastercard prepaid debit cards: Don't get me started! These things are the biggest pain of all. I've had Visa and Mastercard prepaid debit cards and gift cards that wouldn't go through on a purchase on numerous occasions, and by the time I thought to try using them again, they were expired or all the funds had been consumed by monthly service fees. Although legislation has since been passed which outlaws such fees, I still can't stand the idea that the person buying the gift card has to pay an activation charge. Whenever I get these cards, I've now learned to either apply them to my Amazon account (if it actually goes through) or cell phone bill immediately. Amazon: the best thing about Amazon gift cards is that I already buy a lot of stuff from Amazon. In a way, I feel like a sucker for spending so much at Amazon after starting my Prime subscription a couple years ago, but as it happens, Amazon also has the best prices (or close to it) anyway on a lot of the stuff I buy. The only downside to Amazon gift cards (and it's kind of a big one for me) is that it's really easy to unintentionally eat up your gift cards without realizing it. Case in point: the other week I applied a gift card to my Amazon account. A couple days later, I rented a movie, which was charged against my gift card credit. When I went to buy something else, I thought I would be partially paying it with the gift card credit but the amount paid by gift card was less than I expected. I was about to write Amazon's customer service to complain, but then I looked at my gift card history and could see very plainly where the money left. It is because of this purchase history feature alone that I'm comfortable giving Amazon gift cards a 4-star rating. If it weren't for that, I would probably just give them a 3-star rating (at best) because of my overall annoyance with gift cards in general.

title: GOTTA GET A GUND!
text: I bought as many of these as I was allowed at Christmas because as they used to advertise (and maybe still do), you've GOTTA GET A GUND! My son is autistic and when he was small, no toy whatsoever could entertain him but rather a spec of dust could. It was so frustrating because we didn't know he was autistic but definitely knew something (back then it was 1 in 100,000 that you'd have a child with autism, now it's 1 in 50!). In any case, a young officer and his wife are in this fancy toy store one day and dad puts this Gund Polar Bear (looked a lot like this guy) in front of our son's face and suddenly our baby started laughing and giggling and reaching for it. We knew we had to buy it but the price tag was quite high for this young couple--but of course we did. I'd never forgotten that moment--the very first "toy" he loved (there were very few after that but were a few more). Not sure where that fellow landed after all those moves but now he's part of our family again all dressed up in some red. I'm sure there's a grandchild in my future someday that may give all of us another round of loving laughter and giggling but perhaps without the autism but no matter--this fellow brings joy. He's so soft and adorable!

The top part (red) has a middle crease in it so it does not stand up completely, is wrinkled, and bends forward because of the crease. The gift card itself keeps slipping out so I've had to be creative to keep it intact so the "reveal" won't be spoiled when the ornament is opened. Finally, my hanging ornament did not come with a string through the hole as is shown on Amazon and by reviewers in their photos. So I had to find some ribbon and do it myself. That litttle maneuver made the red top part even more loose. The gift card ornament I viewed online was so cute whereas mine is creased and worn looking. This is not my favorite way to present a $75 gift card. I'm sure this was random and I was just the random unlucky recipient of a battered gift card. I'm sure the card itself is good--but the card presentation is a hot mess. Hopefully, if you choose to buy this adorable gift card ornament, you will have better luck and it will be in perfect condition when you get it. If so, it is a winner. That was not my experience.

title: Great Way to Order Morton's Gift Cards
text: Just received two $50 each Morton's Gift Cards that I ordered through Amazon. I actually received them the day after I ordered them--so thanks for that. I admit to being worried about the few bad reviews I read that stated the cards they purchased were bogus and declined at Morton's. So when I got them I did the "scratch thing" on the back of the card to expose the card number, and then I called the "gift card balance" phone number listed on the back of the card, and even talked to a real person--to verify the card balances. They are good. So unless I get a bad surprise from the person I purchased these for, for her August birthday, I think I'm as covered as I can be by pre-verifying the balances on the cards. Ordering gift cards this way is convenient. Morton's is not close to where I live, plus I couldn't find the gift cards at a few stores that I visited. That's why I did this through Amazon. But I really hope that if you purchase a card this way through Amazon, scratch and expose the card numbers and call to ensure validity. It is better for you to verify the cards so if they are bogus, then troubleshoot a problem through Amazon rather than put the gift recipient or yourself through an embarrassing and/or frustrating situation at Morton's.

title: $10 BONUS FOR RELOADING $100 ON GIFT CARD
text: So I've done this several times, if they offer the promotion to you, it should be available to you. I see a lot people disappointed in this offer, but they are referring to their Amazon credit card and it has NOTHING to do with that. This is a prepaid gift card(someone can give you an actual plastic credit card and when you use that, you will start getting these bonus offers. But you DO NOT need to buy or get gifted an actual card. you can just purchase one for any $ amount and it will be sent to your email or text (whatever you enter) and you'll receive a code and when you go to checkout on your next order, there is an option to use gift card. Once you pay for an order with a gift card you will get offers about reloading $ onto your gift card. One thing that may be confusing is that occasionally the reload will not be super instantaneous - it will say "processing" under the status, once that says "applied" you are good to go. The reload shows up as it's own "order" and you will see the balance there on your order + the bonus funds, and will be able to select that as your payment option (it's towards the bottom-you'll have to scroll down if you have a ton of bank & cc options like me). It's a great way to save money, and you can call cust svc to walk you thru it the 1st time if needed.

text: This year my husband and I decided that rather than to go out and spend money on something for my sister and her husband that they probably don't need or necessarily want, that we would do a 'Gift Card' exchange with them. We did get a few laughs out of the realization that we were just basically 'swapping' gift cards in the same agreed upon amount...but decided that we should actually purchase and have the gift cards sent to each other so that we would actually USE them. Just agreeing upon the amount and then relying on ourselves to spend that amount on each of us was just too easy to let slip by and not do. Once the cards were ordered, a very simple process, they arrived very quick. My husband and I have already used ours, with the idea that I will wrap the 'gifts' as they come and they will be opened on Christmas. I know that the cards arrived (in Alaska) to my sister and brother-in-law, not sure if they've 'used' them yet or not. title: Terrible
text: As a long time Amazon.com customer, a gift card seemed like a good purchase. I am just trying to purchase a card to have e-mailed. I basically wanted to convert a Visa debit gift card into an Amazon.com gift card. I put the amount of the card in, the number and expiration date. Amazon accepted it as payment, but after hours of not receiving a confirmation e-mail I checked the site to see what was going on. The site claimed they could not confirm the payment, yet they had already taken money off the Visa gift card. I contacted customer service who told me a Visa gift card is not the best way to purchase an Amazon gift card and they would refund the money to the Visa gift card. I then put in another order using my Amazon.com credit card. A card I have used thousands of times before and never had a problem. This time, I received the same message I got when using the Visa gift card. I contacted Customer Service again. The first person I spoke to told me I had a "Block" on the account. She could not tell me why that was there, and she informed me she could remove it immediately. This claim brought me some concern so I asked to speak with her manager to find out the reason a "Block" had been placed. The manager claimed there was no "Block" on the card and the sale should have gone through fine. So, I again went back and checked on the sale. Again there was a message that it could not be paid using the payment option I had selected. I called back again and told them to cancel the sale. This is extremely disappointing to me, as I have felt for quite some time that Amazon was one of the last customer service oriented sellers around. I guess they too have been pushed to the "Make money, screw the customer" attitude this country has been forced into with our economic situation. A trusted company has gone down the drains. I hope to see you come back to your original ideals some day Amazon.

title: AVOID FRUSTRATION AND READ THIS
text: I buy these cards all the time. They help me with spending issues I've had in the past. They work wonderfully. However, based on a lot of the reviews I've read, it's important you read the info pamphlet so you clearly understand how to go about using it. This will avoid many of the frustrations I read about in other reviews. First, this card can not be used to retrieve cash. Second, if you plan on using it for online purchases you need to register it in your name which will link it to your zip code. When merchants run CC #'s, the 4 main things that need to match with the card are name, card #, zip code and most of the time the CVV # on the back of the card. As long as you registered it correctly any online purchase will always go through assuming there's enough $ on the card. Third, every retailers CC machines operate differently. So, it's important to ask the cashier if their machine automatically subtracts the amount available on the card from your purchase balance or if you need to tell them the exact amount that's on the card so they can manually punch that in before you swipe the card. Asking this will avoid the card from getting declined. If your purchase balance is less then what's available on the card, then you don't need to ask. Also, there's been a handful of times where mine got declined even though I knew I had plenty of funds. I just re-ran the card as debit instead of credit and it works. If you haven't registered your card and need to run it as debit, the pin is the last 4 digits on the card. Fourth, if you purchase items that may hv a chance of being returned, try very hard to keep that card on hand even if it's all used up. Most retailers insist they reimburse your $ bk onto its original form of payment or you'll end up with store credit. There's been many times I went to return and threw out my card already and had to basically make a scene to get cash back. Lastly, never ever ever pay at the pump when getting gas w these types of prepaid cards. There's extra security set up on the CC machine at gas pumps. It knows its a prepaid card, so it will hold all the funds available on your card for probably 7 days. Any retailer that accepts CC has to batch out their machine before any of those funds are deposited into their bank account. This is why they hold the funds. And honestly for whatever reason that I don't understand it seems that these cards can't be used to pay bills online or over the phone. But, that's no fault of the card. That will happen no matter what prepaid card you use. I hope this helps as you scroll along other reviews regarding their troubles they experienced. I believe if you are aware of this then it will help avoid any frustrations and help you determine if this is the right type of card depending on your needs.

title: A GREAT (and SAFER & MORE PRIVATE!) Alternative to Using Your Own Credit Card for Online Shopping!
text: I got this [[ASIN:B01MSBQB1P $100 Visa Gift Card]] because although I have actual credit/debit cards that I use in person at brick & mortar stores and other businesses and online on big-name websites like Amazon, Instacart, Shipt, Target and the like, I am not comfortable giving out my actual card info when shopping on less(er) known and/or potentially risky websites. So when circumstances necessitate doing business with them (as it did recently, while looking for a replacement battery for my 2007 HP laptop I dug out from a closet after not using it since 2009-2010 [and particularly since switching to Apple/Mac in 2012-2013] in order to play some retro offline Windows games I've not played in years that I missed playing................unfortunately, neither Amazon nor any other big-name stores or websites [like Best Buy, NewEgg, etc.] seem to carry a compatible battery and I had to go with an unknown/lesser known website) I prefer to use non-reloadable prepaid "gift" cards, so that in the worst case scenario, if the site is "fly-by-night" scam business and/or the website gets hacked, they won't have access to my actual credit/debit card info or bank data, and the maximum amount of money I'd potentially lose would limited to whatever the denomination (or remaining balance) on the prepaid card. Granted, depending on the card (AFAIK there cards come in denominations of $25, $50, $100 and $200 cards) it could still be a lot of money to lose, but at least one's entire credit line and private info wouldn't be at risk as it would be using a conventional credit/debit card. Personally, after several years of using prepaid Visa, Mastercard and other credit cards, like this one, I have to say I think prepaid "gift" cards are a GREAT option, when shopping online, especially when making purchases at certain websites/kinds of websites. However, previously, Amazon did NOT offer these prepaid Visa, Mastercard and other credit-card "gift" cards and rather, only offered gift cards for specific stores, restaurants or other businesses. This necessitated having to physically go to a brick & mortar store and buy a prepaid "gift" credit card in person anytime I needed a Visa/Mastercard to use online -- and since, due to disabilities, I'm unable to drive, getting these prepaid cards were a huge hassle! Which is why I am so glad that Amazon has started offering these prepaid Visa/Mastercard gift cards for sale through their site. I don't know if its because of COVID-19, and the lockdowns, or what, but making these prepaid cards available through Amazon, has made it a LOT easier for those of us who are mostly homebound, to get and use these cards as needed. As mentioned, these cards come in denominations of $25, $50, $100 and $200, and are NOT reloadable (meaning once the balance on the card is used up, you need to buy another card and cannot add more money to that same card). Also they cannot be used to get cash at ATMs or POS (point of sale) purchases. But they can be made for most other purchases where Visa and Mastercard are accepted, which these days, is the majority of places, at least in the US. I have never used these in other countries, not even Canada, so I cannot speak to their functionality abroad. That being said, I recently tried to use one of these cards online on GOG (Good Old Games) and I had difficulty completing the transaction because apparently the site's based in Europe, so the card was declined. But then I just made the payment using the card as a "guest" via Paypal (I no longer trust Paypal enough to maintain an actual account with them anymore) and the transaction went through, immediately. Other than that, I've had no problems with these cards. The card arrives, open the package and register the card number on their listed website, with your basic info (name, address, phone number, email) which AFAIK is NOT necessary for in-person purchases, but IS (or may be) necessary for online purchases -- and then use the card just like you would any other Visa or Mastercard until you've exhausted the amount on your card. Then, throw it away (or cut it up first if you've registered it with your personal info) and get another one the next time you need it! Easy-peasy! ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ 5 STARS!!!!!!!!!

title: When you apply it, be sure you are sure you want to use it!
text: Two years ago I bought a $50 gift certificate to give my sister. I figured on Amazon she could find something that she'd like and I would not make a bad purchase thus disappointing her. My sister didn't have an Amazon account so had to open one before she tried to purchase something. At that time everything that she added to her cart could not be purchased because it was either not offered directly through Amazon or it was not qualified for another reason. My sister told me of her problems and I told her to not worry to just give me the code and I would give her $50 to use on whatever she wanted. When I tried to apply the code to my account, I discovered it was already used. I ended up having to use my sister's account to make a purchase for myself with the $50 gift certificate. When you apply a gift certificate (even if you don't even use it because your order was not successful!) the gift certificate amount is *fixed* to your account. Therefore, you cannot remove it and give it to someone else. It created a big hassle for me. Make sure that the person you are giving it to will be able to buy something s/he wants. Troublesome.

title: Great addition to options...how about one more?
text: This is a great addition to the various gift card options. Has the look and feel of a store bought gift card plus its value is customizable. Thanks Amazon! I don't know why more companies don't do this. I was first introduced to this concept by "Talbots" so many years ago. Worked out great for last minute and spontaneous gifts. In a pinch for time, I would write the amount on the card, take a photo of the back of the card to capture data, mail it out, then go online that evening to load the card with funds. On one occasion, I sent my elderly Mother a gift card with a marked value of several hundred dollars. I didn't want to worry about it getting lost or misplaced, so I wrote instructions to call me the day prior to use. Worked out perfectly, she actually called me from the store minutes before making her purchases. I went online, loaded the card with funds and Mom was able to use the card minutes later. This is vastly more convenient and secure than buying a gift card at your local store. So safe that you could freely carry these around in your wallet or purse or vehicle for that matter, even with a preselected amount already written on the card (the key is to write the amount on the back of the card as well and take a photo of the back, then use your smartphone to add funds and activate AFTER you've given it out). If you've ever hesitated on sending a gift card to someone because you were concerned that the card may not arrive or be delivered to the wrong address or recipient, this flex card would place your worries aside. If you're sending one of these cards and want to make sure it's received by the intended individual, you could enclose a note instructing the recipient to "call, text or email (your contact information here) to activate this card" OR upon removal of the Amazon activation sticker (on the front of card), you could replace it with your own custom label, instructing recipient on who they need to contact to activate card. You could even add a field on the label for your own security question to recipient, how's that for multiple layers of security. And NOW, my personal wish. When will Amazon be offering gift cards that are charged to the senders credit card at the time of REDEMPTION. (I wonder how many gift card purchases are wasting away in drawers or misplaced across the globe). Of course this would have to come with some notification function (similiar to auto renewal charge of subscriptions) but that would be kind of nice, knowing that your gift had just been used (no other details necessary other than possibly name of recipient) Amazon could be the leader in this "Pay when they Redeem" concept.

First off, they do not work at all in the Pizza Hut mobile app. The app expects a certain number of digits when entering a gift card, and won't accept the number these cards use. (This is as of March 2022... we're not exactly in the early days of online ordering) You CAN add the card to your account on the Pizza Hut website, because it accepts the number format of these cards in addition to the format of cards that the mobile app accepts. The problem, though, is that you can't easily use them later... because 1) the cards you add on the website won't appear in the mobile app as a payment option at all, and 2) if you order on the website and choose a card you previously saved, you're required to re-enter the PIN code from the back of the card anyway. That's incredibly stupid. And, side note, ordering on their website using a phone is a terrible experience compared to using the app. Luckily I held onto my cards "just in case", so when I ran into this issue, I was able to find the PIN code. Otherwise I would have been out $50 from the two cards I added to my account on the website - under the assumption that I could just choose those as my payment method when I ordered from them in the future. title: Value for Money.  Recommended!
text: This is a lovely bear and it is free when you consider that it would cost at least $10 if you purchase it separately. In addition to that, it is a collectible item. I had bought the 2013 (2), 2014 and 2015 collectible bears and got them free when I purchased $65 and $75 worth of toys over the years. Personally, I find that the other bears were more attractive and I even noticed that a few reviewers noted that these bears were faulty and shedding. For now, mine is fine and I love him so much. I do find, however, that he could have been happier as a reviewer noted, after all, it is an intended Christmas present. I sent this gift card with the GUND Holiday 2017 Bear to my brother and he loves it. I do secretly know that he will give my baby the bear as he loves him so much. Anyway, this is a great value and I am very cautious with this bear as I don't want it to fall apart or get ripped off as the ones that were referred to by some reviewers. As you all can see, there is the Amazon log stitched beneath his left paw. The peel-off gift card code is at the back of his ribbon necklace and he also has his matching red hat. I will recommend this gift card with the accompanying GUND holiday bear because if you are already spending more than $100 at Amazon.com, why not take two? I do see that there is a limit of two per customer. Remember that there is no expiration date for your gift card and no attached fees as advertised. I was able to get this to my brother in one day and this is limited to certain locations. text: I purchased several gift cards last year, with greeting cards that had messages suitable to various recipients. Many of my family members are Christians, who appreciate religious-themed cards. This year, there were no such options. They had Hanukkah cards, but nothing mentioning Christmas, let alone anything actually expressing the Christian sentiments about the season! Amazon, like other retailers, makes a good bit of its money off Christmas. I have no problem with them selling cards that are generic, or that relate to holidays of other faiths. I appreciate it, in fact, but I'm a bit offended that they suddenly want nothing to do with the Christian faith or the actual word Christmas. It's like they want the money from the 90% of us who celebrate Christmas, but they don't want to actually acknowledge the holiday or the reason behind it. I usually do almost ALL of my CHRISTMAS shopping with Amazon, but I'll be shopping elsewhere this year, which is a huge hassle. What a bunch of Scrooges.

text: I've had quite a few of these cards. Mostly as presents but I recently bought a few off of another site that was having a $15 off of $75 purchase special. The process only takes about a minute. I usually set up my tee time through the course website like I normally would. Then fill out the form on the Go Play Golf website with all the info from my tee time. The day before I play, I get an email saying that a gift certificate has been bought at the course in my name and then the info of the person at the course. When I check in at the course, I tell them my name and they should have a GC for me. They get it and that's it. Never had a problem in the 25+ times I have used them. I wouldn't buy this for myself without the discount since it wouldn't make much sense but as a gift for somebody else, it is perfect because then they can play whichever course they want. If you have a balance on the card that doesn't cover the cost of a round at the course, you just fill out the request like normal and they will buy a GC in the amount you have left. title: Shady, lying company
text: At first, many people recommended joining the ECA since they're a gaming advocacy group. Recently, however, news about their treatment of members have spread like wildfire. They claimed that the auto-renewal cancellation button on their site does not work, and even claimed that they were unaware about its existence. Several people since have come out with information that the main people at ECA had acknowledged the button months ago, and their statement is obviously a lie. They also baited thousands of people into joining for free, promising them Amazon discounts on games. That discount was discontinued shortly after, and if someone hadn't started this wildfire, thousands of people would have been charged another year of membership because the organization did nothing to contact members who thought they canceled auto-renewal. On top of all that, they require you to send in physical certified mail along with a letter in order to even cancel, claiming they can't process large volumes emails (but somehow can process the same volume of physical mail, which is obviously much more time consuming). On top of all this, none of the members know what ECA is doing or has done, nor would they tell us. Everything added up shows how shady this organization is, and many believe it to be a scam. So save your money, or fund/donate to something actually reputable.
