text: I like the ease of Amazon gift cards, when it comes to the giving and receiving. But I have to agree with the other Prime members. I am sick and tired of watching my gift cards disappear because they are being applied to 1. orders from other members of my household (who don't know to update the order page or have placed orders via the next two methods). 2. Our subscribe and save items. 3. Any digital 1-click purchases. I looked everywhere to find a way to change this method of automatically applying payments to a gift card balance, but unless using the regular check out for certain orders, Amazon does not provide a place to change this payment method. It is automatic. So I never get to use my gifts on myself. Since I'm not alone in this, I don't know if I'll be buying them for anybody with a Prime account or a household that shares an Amazon account in the future. And if I do decide to reload my balance, I'll have to remember the balance likely won't be used to buy myself something nice. But will be used for household purchases, which eliminates a certain amount of convenience and is one of the two reasons I have given this purchase only 3 stars. The other reason is that it took several hours for this reload to be reflected in my gift card balance, though the $5.00 credit I was offered was immediately applied. I am usually very happy with my Amazon purchases and the services I subscribe to. So this is an unfortunate turn of events that I hope Amazon will quickly rectify for all account holders. I doubt very much that Amazon wants its customers to resent the gifts they are receiving through its company.

text: I am a long time prime member with Amazon. I do almost all of my Holiday shopping and the greater part of my regular shopping through Amazon. Last month I received a email gift card from my brother for my birthday. When I attempted to apply the gift card to my account, Amazon advised me that it had already been redeemed. I reviewed all my recent purchases and confirmed that I had not redeemed the card. I attempted to resolve the issue with Amazon but was told that I needed to have the purchaser contact Amazon to resolve the issue. They would not tell me who or how the gift card was spent. My brother argued with Amazon for three days in order to resolve the problem and was ultimately told that he would have to dispute the purchase through his bank. They told him that they could not confirm who spent the gift card or what purchases were made. Both my brother and I are beyond upset. Amazon is a HUGE company who certainly has the resources to resolve the problem with better customer service. Lesson learned - we won't ever buy a gift card from them again. Ultimately Amazon is the one who will miss out. Moral of the story is be very careful when purchasing a gift card from them and don't assume that they will look into a "fraud/theft" and do the right thing for the customer.

text: Obviously, getting a gift card is awesome. And I hate to be one to look a gift horse in the mouth. However, what's the deal with only being able to use an Amazon.com Gift Card on Amazon.com? Why not Amazon.co.uk? This may sound nit-picky, but consider this- just after Christmas, on Amazon.co.uk there was a sale- the "Twelve Days of Kindle" sale. Loads of Kindle Books for real cheap. I got excited, browsed through, chose which ones I was going to use my gift card on, and was set to check out. Looking at the check out page, though, I realized I wasn't going to be able to use the gift card, as it was only good on the US Amazon, not the UK Amazon. I'm not ungrateful- $100 of free books is great, even if there are limitations. But why do those limitations exist? It's the same company, just a different country. I haven't really looked into the legal complications, so perhaps there's a good reason why they legally can't allow us to use both sites. However, to a layman just using the site, it seems a bit unfair that although I'm allowed to buy products from the two (separate, yes, yet identical down to, for all intents and purposes, the logo) sites using the same log-in name, I can't use my gift card on both. Like I said, maybe it's nit-picky. Other than that, though, gift cards are, as one would expect, very good.

I also ordered these little metal wallet cards with greeting card like messages for both boys at the same time I ordered the Visa cards. They have both received these message cards and I am confused at why this is so difficult. How can we be a week and 2 days form when this was supposed to be delivered, and it still has not even shipped? And my orders page says it will be delivered today by 10pm, but it also shows that it has not yet shipped. This has created a very difficult and stressful situation for me as my ex likes to tell the boys that I'm a bad guy and now they think I lied about sending them gifts. A $10 gift card from Amazon won't fix it at this point. I've been a Prime member for at least 10 years. I am Amazon loyal, all of my smart devices, tablets, streaming devices everything is Amazon. I even have Alexa in my car. It seems like lately I'm having issues like this. I'm considering using Insta-cart or Door Dash for my delivery needs. text: You get a free holiday teddy bear with a gift card purchase. Great incentive if you purchase items off Amazon regularly, or plan to give a $100+ gift card to a friend or family member. Supposedly this is the 10th edition of the Holiday Teddy Bear. I started collecting these 2 years ago. Last year was a polar bear with a snow flake santa hat and gloves as opposed to grizzly bear with a Santa hat got this year. Year before that was a darker grizzly bear with a beanie. Hat is not removable (unless you mess with the stitching). There is an ear under there for those wondering. The bear is super soft and huggable. Ideal for toddlers who get attached to soft objects during cold weather. There's also a amazon logo tattoo on it's left foot Gift card is just a neckless attached to the bear. This time, the gift code is a peel off instead of a scratch off in back. Code is very easy to apply with Amazon app, just use the camera feature instead of the traditional input method. Minimum gift card amount is $100. From previous years track record, best to get it early or the lower demonization may sell out Overall if you're going to spend money on Amazon throughout the year or generous enough to give someone a bear + $100+ gift card; then this is a excellent purchase

title: Great show - but get the newer complete set
text: Recently, I was clearing my parents house out and found a box of old toys, including a bunch of Fraggle dolls that I had as a kid. When I mentioned this to my sister, she said she heard that Fraggles were making a comeback with a new movie coming out. Sure enough, when I checked Amazon, the complete series was available. It was such a joy to see this again. This is a great show for kids (or nostalgic adults). The puppetry is great. The show is very musical, but the songs (by and large) aren't corny or annoying. Some of them are actually a bit tender. The episodes often deal with themes like prejudice and the environment. That being said, I'd recommend getting the newer [[ASIN:B002LYD2LW Fraggle Rock: Complete Series Collection]] DVD set. title: It's a gift card...
text: Not sure why I'm reviewing this, but it's in my 'to be reviewed list' so I guess I will. Primarily, this is a gift card shaped like a bookmark. You can use it to mark the location of your last page read in an old-fashioned, paper-paged book. (A 'book' is an archaic item that was around before the advent of the kindle and other e-readers. They routinely chopped down trees, ground them up, and made a pulp mixture. This was used to make paper to print on and bind together. Once bound, they called it a 'book'.) So this can be used to mark your progress as you read a 'book'. Also, you can read the numbers off the back and use it to buy things on Amazon. Once you do that, you can either place it in the circular file, or - - Use it for a straight edge. - Use it as a measuring device (up to it's odd length, and only after you use a marker to write ruler marks.) - Use it to scrape finely chopped things off of a tray. - Use it as a Christmas ornament - Use it as a boundary marker when surveying. - Use it as a conversation starter by hanging it from your bicycle's handlebars. - Use it to scrape snow and ice from your windshield. - And many other uses.

title: Don't believe Amazon promotional ads in the emails
text: I purchased these gift cards as part of a promotion Amazon was running. I will upload a photo of the email I received. In the email it stated "Get $15.00 Amazon credit with a $50 Amazon gift card purchase". It's the end of the school year, so I purchased 3 $50.00 gift card for my kids teachers. I figured that was a great deal for both of us, I spend $35.00 and they get $50.00 for their classroom. Four days later I attempt to purchase a birthday present and was reminded to check on my $45.00 credit I thought I had coming. I couldn't find it, used all their "self help" links, and finally found a phone number to speak to a human and get help. First lady was wonderful, told me the reason I didn't get it was because I had purchased all three in one transaction, instead of 3. I thought that was silly so I asked for a supervisor. The supervisor, Deo located in the Philippines, was the supervisor I was connected to. He informed me what the email really meant was ONE $15.00 credit for purchasing OVER $50.00 in gift cards. Clearly that email is open to interpretation. He said it was written in the terms and conditions...however when I tried to read them for myself I was sent to a different screen (picture attached). I asked to speak with his supervisor, to which he informed me he is the very top of the customer service center. I asked for his boss. He said he was only authorized to give me a mailing address. Dumbfounded I asked him if Amazon corporate office in Washington does not have phones or email. He said they are only allowed to contact them via their computer system. Most of my conversation with Deo was in silence. I'm assuming he was typing up everything I was saying for amazon's records. 54 minutes into my conversation the line disconnected and they never called back. I called back to get amazon's address and was surprisingly connected to a customer service rep who worked in the same department as Deo. He spoke with Deo (who was unable to speak with me since he was busy with another customer). The new customer service rep, Ian, could not have been kinder and more professional. I felt like he was actually listening to my complaint verse Deo who just wanted to record every little thing I said. Ian helped me get the contact information I needed, and also gave me the email address of where I could forward a copy of the email in question. Ian also provided me with the PO Box for Amazon Corporate Office in Seattle. Since I can not voice my compliant to Amazon corporate office directly, and I must write a letter, I figured I would share it with all who would listen. I hope your Amazon experience is better than mine. And Deo, you might want to pay attention to Ian and Mercy - they are customer service pros. Long story short, Amazon - who is worth $430 BILLION - would rather lose a long time customer over $30. But as for the product, it was adorable and looked great in my candy bouquets. I'll attach a picture of that too. ***UPDATE*** After I emailed Amazon as part of a survey they sent, I received the following response: Hello, I understand you're concerned about $15 credit for purchasing $50 gift cards on our website. I can completely understand how frustrating and annoying the situation can be when something like this happens but believe us it was never our intention. After reviewing your previous correspondences with our customer service, I can confirm the information provided to you was correct. As my colleague mentioned, the promotional credit will be provided only one per customer. You can view the restrictions for promotion code here: http://www.amazon.com/promos I realize this is frustrating; however we aren't able to offer any additional insight or action on this matter and any further inquiries regarding this issue won't receive a response. We appreciate your understanding. Best regards, Madhan P. Amazon.com I did go to that link, and there is nothing that addresses my concern or complaint. I wrote back asking them to highlight the part that actually has to do with my complaint. Don't worry, I'll update this if they ever respond.

title: There is Zero Reason to Dislike This Or To Pay WIth Another Method
text: I never just buy things with my debit/credit cards directly. Amazon gives you 2% more purchasing power if you use a debit card and have linked your checking account to your Amazon account, and then use that card to reload with. Literally- LITERALLY- they are giving you $2 per $100 for FREE. The process is also as straight-forward and streamlined as one could realistically demand (I guess it'd be better if it sensed when and how much I wanted to load telepathically and then immediately did it, but only slightly). For some, this route will help them conserve money and foster/impose financial self-discipline. You can designate only so much to spend per month on Amazon, and see at a glance how much you have left. (Of course, the ease with which you can add more if you want to go over budget undermines this potential purpose if you already completely lack self-discipline.). If you have a household member, you could give them an allowance of sorts via this method, too, I reckon. But the sole reason I pay with my Amazon Gift Card 100% of the time is the 2% boost to my purchasing power. When you're poor (even when you're not: why'd you not take a 2% boost that is so trivally easy even if you were Trump or Bezos?), these sorts of bonuses can be more impactful than the low % might seem upon perfunctory reflection. The discounted Prime for being low-income is also nice. Thanks, Amazon! (that said, stop being a jerk about paying taxes and employees- everyone else matters, too)

Not that the expense isn't clear--it's more my habit to pay cash for little, everyday expenses and hold my cards for larger things only--like tv's. title: Fast shipping overseas, well packaged, great gift idea!!
text: I don't like buying gift cards for Christmas as it's not really all that meaningful, but I'm deployed overseas so I thought it'd be the easiest way to get my family a simple but meaningful gift this year. I had the gift cards mailed overseas so I can add my own personal message in the card before mailing them back to the states. Obviously I didn't get one day shipping but it was ALOT faster than I expected. It arrived by the end of the week. Usually orders take 2-3 weeks before delivery. The only thing I was slightly displeased with (although really nobody's fault) is that on the customs label it clearly stated "Amazon gift card, valued at $250" which could cause a higher risk for "getting lost in transit" but that wasn't the case. The card was very well packaged. I was worried about the card getting slightly bent in transit as its coming from overseas and making a lot of stops along the way. The card and envelope were enclosed in a larger sealed envelope inside a small box with bubble wrap type padding. All-in-all, great gift idea, plenty of room to write a personal message, fast shipping, A+ Amazon!!

title: These are not Apple Store gift cards, they're Apple App Store gift cards
text: I use apple devices all the time, but I wasn't overly familiar with Apple gift cards. I typed in "Apple store gift cards" into Amazon, and it showed me this. I bought it as a gift. It turns out the person wanted "Apple store gift cards" (as I typed in), but these are "Apple App Store & iTunes gift cards). I didn't realize there was a difference. I figured it's the same company, how could there be two separate ones? Surely they are interchangeable or convertible. WRONG! They definitely CANNOT be used interchangeably. I contacted support to see if I could do something to fix this (I read in forums of people converting them over via Apple support). So I did all the stuff the support site said to do, submitted the request. Then they got back to me and said since I bought them from Amazon, not directly from Apple, there was no way for them to convert them over for me. So I'm stuck with $250 dollars of app store and itunes credit and the person I bought these for (and myself) rarely ever buy anything from that. So yay! Flushing money down the toilet! And for reference, you CAN use xbox and microsoft store gift cards interchangeably. And no, I'm not an xbox/ms fanboy. I like apple devices, but this situation is bs. If you want to avoid all this bs, read up on the difference between apple store and apple app store gift cards and buy them directly from Apple or don't buy them at all. Don't buy them on Amazon because it limits your recourse if something goes wrong as I learned the hard way. I consider myself pretty knowledge on most digital matters, but I failed on this one. I pity the poor grandparent or other less-knowledgeable individual that has to deal with this. Two thumbs down.

All changes to your files are made in real-time thus preventing the additional steps of manually updating everything in different locations. Great for collaboration as well. I have shared folders with my colleagues that all of us work on. One major drawback of Dropbox: multiple users cannot simultaneously work on a shared file (like you can Google Drive). text: Okay, amazon... I appreciate that I can buy these at low denominations and without additional fees. Therefore, I get that these are flimsy, easy to make cards subject to bending. What I don't get is why you would send a bunch of flimsy cardboard cards without a backer board in the shipping envelope? I ordered four of these gift cards as Christmas presents, and every single one of them has a visible (ugly) crease in them. I am glad they are only going to close family who I know will be able to laugh at amazon's failures because this would be embarrassing otherwise. I also am very glad that I ordered different designs for each person, and the same dollar amount for the one duplicate I had....otherwise, it would have been a nightmare trying to figure out which card had which dollar value. I did read in the description that there is no dollar amount on the card itself, and can understand this being a possible good thing when gifting, but there must be something you can do for gifter so they can tell which is which! I can only hope that they are redeemable with no problems once the recipients get them. (I will update my review accordingly.) But for now, if nothing else, definitely, DEFINITELY send them with a backer board!! (or in a cardboard envelope)

They suggested that I contact Starbucks to get this fixed, but this is NOT Starbucks' fault or responsibility (they did not sell me the cards). If you read the negative reviews for this product, you will see that I am not the only one that has received gift cards that were empty, after people paid for them. I am surprised that Amazon continues to knowingly sell these gift cards that are shipped empty/not activated.

title: Make sure you have your zip code on your account or you might be spending hours trying to activate
text: I spent many hours working with a friendly, but not so helpful Spotify email support. I sent 7 emails and got 7 responses from them. They tried hard to resolve my issue, I will give them that. My gift card purchased here from Amazon would not activate with the error "Something went wrong. Try again or get help." I got relatively fast email support from Spotify. After several screenshots and proving I made the purchase by sending them a picture of my Amazon receipt, they first thought the missing zip code on my account was the problem. Later, someone wrote that they would activate it if it didn't work after I tried again on another computer. I tried on my main, PC, and Ipad, and my Iphone web browsers. You cannot activate a gift card through their app. It turns out the Spotify servers have a number of times you can try a code a day, and the support staff say they cannot reset the count. I tried the next day and my code worked perfectly without any issue on my main computer's web browser where I started in the first place. Lesson learned after hours of frustration: check your address is right on file with your zip code, then try to activate the card you buy from Amazon. Support cannot help you if you tried your code too many times.

title: no more lost or forfeit gift cards...
text: I make most purchases here with a credit card, so the Amazon Gift Card is not a regular payment method for my routine purchases. What it *does* provide me is a dumping ground for almost every other hard to use gift card — presents, store refunds, promotional rebates, participation incentives, etc. It can be a pain to track a pile of cards, which can expire, are hard to drain of "change" from a partial use, and some merchants will discourage or refuse a split payment. I've lost significant money to those challenges, and spend too much emotional energy trying to avoid the traps. Now I immediately dump any gift card I receive into the Amazon card, knowing that sooner or later I will have a purchase to make. No lost cards. Nothing lost to fees or expiration or loose change. No problem with use limitations. Yay! It is also a faster way to receive credit for returns to Amazon than waiting for the bank to issue credit, or having 3rd-party vendors complicate the process. The gift card is automatically the default payment choice for my next purchase — so I don't forget and have money sitting in an unused credit. But if I *don't* want to use it (from a different budget category, or money I owe to somebody else), I can change the default choice and hold the gift card balance for whatever time or purpose. The process is sort of not intuitive and it's easy to lose where things are on the Amazon site, but once figured out it's swell. I would take a rating star or half star for ease of use — but I know of no alternative with similar utility, so it sits at the top of its class. However many stars that should be.

title: Too many restrictions
text: Only a select group of Spotify subscribers can use their gift cards (read: only full price standalone Premium subscription months). They cannot be redeemed for the family or student plans. Additionally, other terms apply, which includes any offers that combine Premium with other products or services (like the free Hulu bundle). I don't know many people who are aware of someone's subscription details before they buy a gift card (do you know your co-worker's billing details?). So, unfortunately, many gift cards are unable to be used. The reasoning behind the restrictions is a mystery. Wouldn't it make sense for students on Student Plans to be given a gift card to help them pay for their music service? Most gift cards are seen as cash in the form of credit for a particular place. If the subscriber is paying X dollars/month for the service and they are given X dollars in a gift card form, why isn't it accepted by the same company who is putting the cards out there? After 3 years of seeing gift cards wasted among friends, colleagues, and family, and seeing the online complaints mount urging Spotify to change their restrictions while nothing changes, I've vowed to never touch them again. Just give cash.

text: We had a secret Santa exchange at work this past Christmas. The person who drew my name came onto Amazon and bought one of these cards for me because they'd seen some of the older merchandise I had on my desk that had the original ThinkGeek logo and website information on it. I thanked the person who got it for me and she asked what I intended to buy from the website. I had to explain that ThinkGeek no longer existed, because Gamestop had purchased it and essentially phased out the ThinkGeek line of items. She was HIGHLY upset that Amazon was still selling gift cards for a store and website that didn't exist. She said it was shameful of Amazon to cheat people out of their money by selling a product that couldn't even be used. She commented that if she'd wanted to buy a gift card for Gamestop, she WOULD have, but she KNEW that Gamestop wasn't a store I would even shop from because I'm not a video game player. After our LONG discussion, she asked for the card back and said she was going to give it to her teenage son. However, after her son went to try to use it later, Gamestop REFUSED to take the card! So whomever is saying that this card can be used at Gamestop, they've apparently never TRIED to use it there. My coworker ended up contact the BBB about this scam gift card and how it was STILL being sold, despite the fact that it couldn't be used anywhere. So she's STILL trying to get her money back, but she bought me a new gift card anyway. However, she decided to get a general gift card that could be used almost anywhere and not for a specific store. She did also state that she would NEVER buy another gift card from Amazon.

title: Please stop showing me $10 off $100 advertisements when I don't qualify.  Don't be evil.
text: The rules for the $10 off $100 deal which is widely advertised include the provision that it is only good on the first time one has reloaded a gift card. I did that years ago before these advertisements started appearing, so I only qualify for $5 back on $100 which is the same as my amazon credit card so no benefit to me in going through the hassle of locking myself into the gift card reload. In my more vulnerable mindstates, I have fallen for the "Oh, I'll just quickly reload my gift card before checking out to get the offer they are telling me is available". Only recently did I spend the 15 minutes of so that it took me to dig into the rules of the offer to realize that I was only getting 5% back. And they make the process of getting $10 on $100 pretty opaque, with different payment options giving different rebates, IIRC splitting 10% up into two 5% credits at different times, which tends toward making someone who is only getting 5% back think they will get another 5% later on because that's what amazon said. This is by far the most user-unfriendly user interface design I have seen on amazon, and feels like an indication that they have gained the monopoly power to stop being user-centered and start being evil. Don't jump the shark amazon; stop showing the ad to people who don't qualify. And when people who don't qualify try to get the offer, be clear to them that they are not getting the offer.

title: You gotta read the fine-print and know what you're getting...
text: You gotta read the fine-print. It states on the product page and on the card itself that these must be redeemed online and not in-theater. Fandago is a third-party service, so you can't use their gift-cards in-theater. It's a pain... but at the same time, it's a little ridiculous reading all these complaints from people who can't be bothered to actually research what they're buying. That should just be something you do, regardless. If you want a gift-card to use in-theater, you gotta get the theater-specific gift-cards. Not a third-party card produced for use on a specific website. The convenience fee's are steep, but that's where their profit comes from, so I can't complain too much. Running a service like this isn't free. And a lot of theaters offer promotional offers or rewards programs that can cut down or even eliminate fees. Problem is, these cards aren't perfect and the customer service is pretty mediocre, so you can run into problems pretty easily. If you encounter a problem and are having trouble with Fandango, I'd also recommend calling your local theater and explaining the situation calmly. (Aka, don't throw a fit, since the theater and Fandango are not the same thing.) It's possible that if you can't get help from Fandango, the theater might be able to swap your tickets for another time/movie at the very least, or work out another solution. On the whole, I really don't recommend Fandango cards. It's a lot easier, and sometimes cheaper, to just get cards for your specific theater, since they usually sell tickets on their own website.

text: Here's the scam. They will offer a promo, but when you reload for the first time Amazon flags it as fraud & puts your account on hold & cancels the order. By the time you get back into the account, and reload with their permission it is no longer a first time reload, because there was an order processed & cancelled by them so the promo is no longer available to you. I tried to add $200 to card that I received as a gift after spending... First time reload- said it was processing, received an e-mail that they put my account on hold for suspicious activity & cancelled all pending orders. I needed to reset password. I called customer service, they apologized & said it was for my safety... told me all was good now. Second try...said it was processing, received an e-mail that they put my account on hold for suspicious activity & cancelled all pending orders. I need to reset password. I called customer service and they asked my why the last CSR didn't file a report with fraud. I don't know?! They told me I cannot access my account until fraud reviews it the next day. text: Panera Bread is a bakery and café with locations all across the United States. This is definitely one of those places where there is a little something for everyone. It used to be considered a "hipster" establishment, but is now definitely one that everyone frequents. There is a bakery where you can select fresh-bakes breads, pastries, and other desserts to either take home or snack on in-store in the dining area. You can order from a variety of soups, salads, and sandwiches to enjoy in the spacious dining areas complete with fireplaces and jazzy music. The Quick Gift envelope the gift card came in said $100 Mastros Thousand Oaks (CA). In January I dined at Mastro's When the bill came I gave the waiter my Amex Card and the Landry's Multibrand gift card. When the waiter returned he said, "Landry's hasn't put us on their gift card system yet, so I put the whole amount on your Amex Card". I asked to speak to the manager. The manager confirmed what the waiter told me. Then asked to see the gift card. I gave it to him and he wnt to a phone and checked the balance. When he came back he said the card had a zero balance. When I got home I called the balance checking number and discovered the card still has a $100.00 balance. i wrote a letter of complaint to Landry's corporate office and followed up with two telephone calls. Landry's never called me back. Yesterday I called two nearby Morton's Steakhouses to see if I could use my gift card at Morton's. In both cases the person on the other end of the phone told me I could not use the gift card at Morton's, because, "Landry's hasn't put us on their gift card system yet."

text: I usually (won't anymore) upload my VISA gift cards that I receive to Amazon for use online. I did this with just over $350 last month. I did a "Reload" with this $350. It was there. It showed in my account. With the funds clearly showing I made my purchases that equaled about $355. When I checked out, the cart clearly, and I repeat CLEARLY showed that $350 would be used from my Amazon Gift Balance and $5 from my debit card. Well, you guessed it, that did NOT happen. Amazon whacked my bank card for $355 and refused to find a solution other than putting the money back on the gift cards. On the surface that seems reasonable but it isn't. It caused a great hardship for me as it was NOT in my budget to spend $350 out of my checking that way. Of course the gift cards were again usable but I can't use a gift card to pay my mortgage. Thanks a lot Amazon for putting the financial squeeze on me. It was absolutely unacceptable that Amazon wouldn't put the money back into my bank account and figure out how to transfer that transaction to the Gift Balance that I uploaded to Amazon. I was on the phone for just over one hour with the Amazon representative who was either ruefully ind adequately trained or just plain stupid, not sure which but this situation has me hesitant to even remain as a Prime customer. SHAME ON YOU AMAZON.

title: Gift cards and promotions - do not mix!
text: Original review- I recently bought a $500 gift card of this type to take advantage of the 2019 Prime Day "Buy More, Get More" promotion through the Amazon App on my iPhone. Although I carefully followed all terms and conditions of the promotion, the credit didn't appear in the app when it should have. I spent over 3 hours of back and forth with customer service, only to ultimately be rejected for "not buying through the Amazon App", which I was very careful to do, but how could I prove that? Meanwhile, others in my exact same situation got their promotional credits with less trouble. Usually Amazon customer service has been great to me in the few times over the years I've had to call them. Maybe I just got bad customer service reps, so I'm writing this review in hopes that someone who won't accuse me of lying will reach out to me about the issue. I'll definitely change this review to reflect anything that happens. Either way though, the only lesson I can take from this whole situation is: do not trust promotions from Amazon (especially ones that involve these gift cards), and definitely don't trust customer service to do the right thing without a bunch of trouble. It seems that Amazon has really changed, and not for the better. EDIT: 7/31/2019 So, I just checked the Amazon App (ahem... where I bought this gift card), and when I looked in the notifications, I saw one for the promotional credit I should have gotten, which was credited on 7/30 and which expires on 8/7. I was able to redeem it without a problem. I guess one of the higher ups at Amazon got many (if not all) the affected customers their credits, albeit with only 9 days to redeem them (7/30-8/7) instead of the 12 days they should have had (7/19-7/31). Still though, this whole experience has left a bad taste in my mouth. I understand other customers may be more important than me and therefore they get their problems solved quicker and easier, but the $3000+ I spend on Amazon every year should be worth fixing the most egregious errors like this one, no? And to basically be called either stupid or a liar by customer service, when I'm pointing out clear errors, is kinda inexcusable. 3 stars for the problem being finally fixed, but CS and the marketing/promotions team clearly have some work to do.

title: Give up on the lottery, buy these shims instead
text: I used to play the lottery three times a week, but then I found these! This gift card is amazing. I got it for a friend to level a wobbly table and it was the perfect thickness. My friend noticed that there was a scratchy lotto game on the back and we went to Amazon to see if we had won. There is a special section under “my account” where you can enter the code. It turns out we won $50, which is exactly what I paid for the leveling device. Since then I have bought about ten more, and all of them were basically a free ticket. We haven’t hit the big one yet, but there’s not a single chair on my block with a rock. One important thing to note... whether you buy the $25, $50, or $100 version all are the same thickness, so two $25 shims are not the same thickness as a $50 shim, but the prize has consistently matched the price. If you have a large gap to fill, it would be much more cost efficient to buy small denomination shims. I’ve started to wallpaper the kid’s room with them now, but am having a hard time finding new things to spend my winnings on. P.S. The included envelopes are great for fine adjustments but shouldn’t be used in places where moisture may be a problem, like under the fridge.

title: Duplicate orders caused confusion this year
text: I purchase Amazon Gift cards every year during Christmas and they always arrive promptly and attractively packaged. This year, however, something happened and I received two boxes of gift cards on the same day, duplicate orders. I assumed that there was a processing glitch at Amazon and that only one of the orders of cards was valid. I received no communication from Amazon conveying which order was the good order, and couldn't determine which was the good order without activating the cards myself (and this wouldn't work, as they aren't transferable after activation). So I took a chance and gave out a set from one of the boxes and held onto the other set just in case. As my luck would have it, when my nephews and nieces tried to use the cards, they didn't work. The gift cards I gave out were the invalid ones. Fortunately, my nephews and nieces are good kids and they knew I would make it right. So, through the help of my sister-in-law and a lot of time texting, we got the good card information to the kids. Even though it all worked out in the wash, Amazon certainly could have made it a lot easier with one little email. I'll definitely have to reassess my gift card purchases next year.

text: To be honest this is the most insecure function of Amazon or any other online store that I have ever seen, and I have never even used it personally. This is the THIRD time that I have had to report fraudulent purchases on my account to Amazon support that were made through their online gift card feature. The first time it was $300 and the two more recent ones were $100 each. Every time I have had to report the breach and have Amazon or my bank refund the purchase and reset the account. I have two factor authentication turned on, have changed my password multiple times and during this most recent breach even I did not have access to the account. After the second breach I had Amazon temporarily disable the account and reset the password randomly, so that even I didn't know what the password was. And STILL someone managed somehow to access the account and charge money to the online gift card. Honestly at this point I am getting frustrated enough to just stop using Amazon completely and destroy my account. And I know for a fact that my computer and my phon AND my email have not all three been hacked at the same time. The two factor authentication on my phone isn't even connected to the internet. It's a randomly generated code that is changed every few seconds, so the only way to even get the code is to have access to my phone itself. There has to be some kind of back door that someone is using to get to the account and reload the gift card balance. And it's only the gift card that seems to be the issue because they aren't making purchases directly with the card on file. Whatever this issue is Amazon needs to resolve it ASAP, as it is a major security issue.

It’s no longer worth my time or effort and I’m pretty sure it cost VISA way more than $100 to pay their reps for all the time they wasted on the phone with me. (That makes me feel a little better)! title: Hidden fees and a Hassle to use - AVOID !!
text: I have received Fandango cards two times in a row (from the same person that knows I am a movie nut) for Christmas. And while I HATE to be that guy who complains about a gift, I'm going to have to tell the person to please stop giving me these cards. I'll break it down for you, the potential buyer here on Amazon who is thinking about buying the movie nut in your family one of these practically useless cards. 1. You can't just take the card into a theater and pay for a movie, like you would with any other type of gift card, in any store. 2. You HAVE to purchase your tickets on your laptop or desktop computer, planning ahead and hoping nothing comes up to make you miss your showtime. 3. You CAN'T use your smart phone with these cards. Many gifts cards I've seen, you just scan the number on the back and it loads your card into the app for whatever store or service the card is for, like Starbucks or iTunes does. 4. You can create an account on Fandango but you CAN'T just load your gift card amount into your "account bank" because there is no such feature on their website. 5. You have to use the card for each ticket you purchase, for a specific time and place, and there is a "convenience" charge (the amount depends upon the theater chain - the one chain in my city that actually accepts these cards charges $1.30 for EACH TICKET (not just for each transaction.) 6. You get a numbered code either in an email or a printable ticket (I've never used the the printable ticket, I've been told it's a nightmare) and go to the kiosk outside said theater and use the numbered code to get your actual ticket. 7. Once you realise you have only 2 or 3 dollars left on the card, it's pretty much useless, because THAT 2 or 3 dollars is going to taken up by the "convenience fee" Fandango charges you to use their gift card. In short, a $25 Fandango Gift card I got that should get me at least 4 tickets (we always go to matinees and they are only $6.00 each - hell, our theater has $5.00 Tuesdays every week that we take advantage of, and that would be FIVE tickets!) gets me 3 tickets (or only two if we go at night) and a few dollars left on a card I know I won't use. If you're gonna give someone a gift of movie tickets, Just hand them 25 dollars in cash and say "Go out and enjoy a few movies."

text: I needed to spend some money on a credit card that has a UK billing address, which can be difficult as a lot of online stores don't allow foreign billing addresses. And most sites that sell Visa gift cards also don't accept foreign billing addresses themselves. But Amazon does, so I bought this Visa gift card on Amazon, paid for it with the UK card, problem solved. I didn't use this card in any physical stores, so I can't speak to that experience. I received it today, immediately registered it at the URL that's on the back of the card (top right, small text). You need to register it online first to be able to make purchases with it online (this is how you set your name and billing address on it, which you would need for any online order). I then used it on Etsy.com and Mouth.com for purchases that came close to the $100. I then used it to reload my Amazon gift card balance in the amount that I had left. I then checked my balance again at the same website where I had registered it, and indeed it showed my three transactions and correct zero balance. No problems at any point.

title: Beware Cinemark Gift Cards and your personal data when registering them online
text: This is an account of a movie theater company, Cinemark inc., and their failure to provide customer service as well as recognize a data breach. On June 21, 2019, I reached out to their customer service line, spoke to their rep. Janine, and advised that my Christmas Gift to my wife, a Cinemark gift card, was showing a zero balance in error. I sent screenshots of the original gift card receipt as well as screenshots while logged into my Cinemark account showing the card registered. They opened case G5446965, identified that the card's remaining balances of $37.01 was used in California on May 10, 2019 (which neither my wife nor I were there) and then said that gift cards were treated as cash and Cinemark was not liable to any theft. After the call was completed, I told my wife this information and asked her if she ever used the card OTHER than the Cinemark.com website, where we registered the gift card under our cinemark.com account. She stated she did not. This clarified that this meant that my Cinemark.com account had been hacked and that Cinemark SHOULD be liable because their security breach is what caused the remaining balance to be stolen from the gift card. I called back and Cinemark Supervisor Talisha who opened case Gs0405267 where I requested a new gift card with the stolen balance $37.01 sent to me, I requested my account be deleted from their data, and that Cinemark corporate contact me to discuss their measures to protect my data that was hacked from their website. Time and life go by and I call back 7/5/19 and speak to supervisor Ashley, who says the previous case was closed in error, and opens new case GS0425458 on July 5th. She assured me that the replacement gift card would be mailed, that my account would be deleted from the Cinemark Website, and that a member of Cinemark would call me to discuss my stolen data from their website. I advised I would give them until July 29th to honor this promise, otherwise I would post my story public , describing the failure of Cinemark to honor promises from THREE supervisors to contact me regarding the data breach as well as replace the stolen (from the Cinemark website) funds. As of today, I have not received any call from any representative from Cinemark, My account remains active on the Cinemark.com website, and the promised replacement gift card was never received

title: Just want to share my horrible experience of using Netflix giftcards
text: DO NOT buy Netflix Gift Card!! It's not the same as regular payment! I have been a Netflix user for a long time and I would buy gift cards for myself at times since I thought it's the same as credit card payment anyways. However, I did not realize there is one big disappointing surprise of using these gift cards.. What happened is that I will be traveling abroad for a few months and was hoping to put my account on hold in the meanwhile and will resume my membership after I come back. However, I was told that the only way to put my account "on hold" is to cancel my membership and reactivate when I come back. However, when I clicked the cancel membership button, I was told that my membership will only be canceled after all of my credit are used up. I still have more than $48 dollars of credit from previous gift card purchase and having my accounting charged for the next 4 months completely defeats the purpose of canceling my account which is to put it on temporarily hold without getting charged. I called the help center and the lady told me there is no way to put my account on hold without getting charged since I have purchased gift cards. I told her it makes no sense as it seems I am being "punished" for pre-depositing money at Netflix by using giftcards, which she agreed! she then said she'll talk to her team to see if they can help. To my big surprise, after being put on hold for 10+ minutes, instead of helping with a solution, she came back reading a bunch of terms and agreements that I "agreed" when I sign up, essentially saying "this is what you agreed to, even though I agree it makes no sense, but we're legally protected" anyways, really frustrating experience. one thing for sure is that I will not being resuming my membership after my credit runs out! Just want to share my horrible experience of using Netflix giftcards. so please be aware. Thanks.

title: Card ok if you can put up with Amazon.com customer service
text: If you've never had a problem shopping from Amazon.com, then you really are not experienced enough to be giving the "gift" of Amazon to someone else. Wait until you've experienced your first screw up, and then evaluate. I received a gift certificate, but have had trouble using it, because Amazon.com's outsourced customer service does not handle issues well. They are apparently scripted to say that an appropriate person will contact you within 48 hours, but in my experience, follow up contact is not timely. When contact is made, it has been to tell me that the issue was not well documented by the prior agents and to start over explaining my concern once again. After that, I was told, once more, to wait 48 hours for follow-up that did not come. Rinse and repeat. The problem is that Amazon.com has apparently fire-walled these folks in Bangalore (or some other asian town) from the rest of the company. Therefore, there can be no quick responses to customer concerns. For me, after five contacts, I spoke with a "team lead" who indicated that prior agents had not documented the subject matter of my prior calls (even though I was promised a pompt resolution by those agents). Add to all this the fact that during the recent holiday season, Amazon.com raised the price of the item I wished to purchase more than once, at the same time that the item's manufacturer was offering it for considerably less. This makes having my "gift" money tied up in an Amazon.com account less than ideal. Do not expect that the person to whom you intend to give a gift will not have to deal with the customer service department. Try to be forward-thinking enough to consider that a problem might occur. If it does, the recipient will likely have a very negative experience, regardless of the variety of products offered by Amazon.com. When I asked an Amazon.com customer service agent why Amazon.com was charging 150% of what the manufacturer was selling the product for directly, I was told that the additional expense should be considered to cover the expert customer service available at Amazon.com. This is terribly amusing, considering that the only thing that the agents tend to do is instruct the customer to wait 48 hours for someone else to address the problem (which, in my experience, does not happen). If you are set on letting someone choose their own gift, you should consider a pre-paid Visa or Mastercard. That way, the recipient could use the funds at Amazon.com if he or she so chooses, and is still free to purchase something locally from a person who could not avoid responding to a customer's concerns.

text: Be prepared that very few people at Hyatt know how these giftcards work. I've tried to use several giftcards at several locations on several different occasions, and each time, every Hyatt employee I've encountered (over the phone or in person) have to put me on hold and call corporate to figure out how to redeem them. I'm literally sitting on hold right now trying to book an advanced reservation with one now and they can't seem to figure out how to apply a $100 gift card to a $500 reservation. (15 minutes and counting). This is the third time I've tried to use it. The answer I just received is "you can't use a gift card on an advanced booking rate"----different answers with different hotels. When I call the same hotel later tonight, I will get a different answer. At a different hotel 2 months ago, they nearly lost their minds because first they said you couldn't use them in international hotels (wrong) and then they said you can only use one gift card per stay (also wrong---after calling corporate for 1 hour, they took them all). Long story short: you will experience resistance, confusion, and stress every time you try to use one---especially if you try to use more than one. One thing to keep in mind: The FULL balance of your giftcard has to be used---ie: if you have a $200 balance and your booking is only $100, you will not be able to use the giftcard. Your giftcard will pay for anything on your folio, however (ie: spa treatments, meals, room service, etc). Hope this helps.

title: Rest Assured, This Is Indeed a $25 Gift Card in a Black Gift Box
text: At first, I was skeptical. Would this gift card be exactly $25? What if they only gave me $24.75 and tried to pull it off as $25? What if the box wasn't the right shade of black? Was it going to be jet black, onyx, or obsidian? Would the bow be off-center? To be honest, it looked a little off-center in the photo. What if I went to type in the gift card code, lost my memory, forgot how to operate a keyboard, and never recovered my hard-earned money? We've all had these doubts -- it's only human. I'm happy to say that the bow -- just gold enough to hint at prestige with a touch of yellow that says "I'm also fun!" -- was immaculately placed. I assume machine learning was involved (God bless you, Mr. Bezos). The interior of the box, which may look to be little more than black cardboard, is in fact black cardboard covered in a thin, felt-like veneer. Teasing the card from its luxurious case, I scratched away the code with my full mental faculties intact. At last, 408 digits later, the screen read "$25.00". Not $24.75, not $24.95, but a full twenty-five American dollars. It is no exaggeration to say that, if only for a moment, my faith in humanity has been restored.

title: Popcorn tin or Amazon gift card?  Amazon wins hands down.
text: What's that? You forgot to get a gift for the cousin that you never see but who will be present at the holiday gathering? You pulled Bob's name in Secret Santa and you know nothing about Bob? You detest shopping? Look no further than this handy ten pack of Amazon gift cards. Here are some facts about the gift cards: 1)What would I be handing to my gift recipient? These gift cards are the traditional plastic kind. Also note that Amazon sells gift cards in various formats. You can get gift certificates that you print at home, e-gift cards delivered via Facebook, and e-gift cards delivered by email. 2)How are the gift cards packaged? You get a stack of ten cards that come in a single, fully closed (non-zipper) plastic bag that must be torn open in order to remove the cards. My stack of gift cards arrived in a nondescript bubble wrap mailer. 3)Does the buyer receive envelopes or greeting cards? You receive no envelopes and you receive no greeting cards. Amazon does have an option where you can buy a single gift card that comes with an envelope and greeting card. Look here: [[ASIN:BT00CTOUNS Amazon.com Gift Cards - In a Greeting Card - Free One-Day Shipping]]. If you want a pack of gift cards that also come with multiple envelopes, Amazon has that, too. Look here: [[ASIN:B005Z3E8NC Amazon.com Gift Cards, Pack of 10 Cards in Greeting Cards - Free One-Day Shipping]] 4)What designs are available? I chose the generic design with the "a" because this enables me to use the cards beyond the 2011 holiday season. The designs on the gift card vary. For this ten pack, Amazon presently offers relatively limited card designs. There is a generic snow globe and a card that says "Happy Reading" and another that says "Thank You". If the look of the plastic card is important, you will have more options to choose from by purchasing one of the single card options here: [[ASIN:BT00CTOUNS Amazon.com Gift Cards - In a Greeting Card - Free One-Day Shipping]]. 5)How quickly do the gift cards arrive? These cards come quickly. I ordered on a Saturday night and they arrived on Monday. 6)How much money is loaded on each card? Each of the ten cards is loaded with $10. If you want gift cards that are loaded with more money, Amazon has a couple of gift card pack options of different monetary amounts. Do you need a smaller pack of gift cards? More than one but less than 10? You can get packs of three cards preloaded with $15, $25, $50, and $100 by looking here:[[ASIN:B005Z3D5OU Amazon.com Gift Cards, Pack of 3 Cards - Free One-Day Shipping]]. Note: the three pack does not presently come with envelopes. In sum, you cannot go wrong with these cards. Keep a stash of these cards in the preloaded monetary amount of your choosing so you are always prepared when you need to provide a gift and don't have time and/or the desire to shop.

I didn't want to destroy the outer envelope for fear that was Amazon's intended packaging for the gift card. The brief fret was unnecessary. Amazon has the large sealed envelope protecting another envelope and a card. The gift card is attached to the card (the presentation is pretty much like the photo on the product page). The gift card itself was a hard plastic card. I don't know if Amazon still issues its paper gift certificates but this is a definite improvement as it is less prone to damage by water or tearing. A nice gift that is well packaged.

title: ELEGANT TIN
text: I received this item today and boy, was I pleasantly surprised! What an elegant looking tin. It's a lovely presentation for a gift card. It's bigger than I thought it would be at "5-1/8" X "3/8". It's a stocking stuffer for my husband but I suspect we will probably hold onto it afterward and use it to give another gift card to someone next year. It's that nice. That said, there are some things I should clarify, one being the free shipping. Amazon advertizes free one day shipping but when you place the order the confirmation says free two day shipping. This didn't matter to me. Hopefully, I am never in a position where it will. I ordered the afternoon of Dec. 17th, and it was at my door in 48 hours. Impressive. I am not complaining about getting a free gift tin and free expedient shipping, I simply want to point it out. It's somewhat confusing and deceptive. The other point I wanted to make was about a message you can include with your order. Don't bother. It's simply a note written on the packing slip. If you need to address the gift or feel compelled to jot something down, might I suggest adhering a gift tag to the underside of the tin. Why do they have slots cut out of the bottom of the tin? I suspect it has something to do with being able to scan the card's bar code. Anyway, if you need to put a tag on it that's where I would do it. I considered rating this item only 4 stars because of these two issues, but I truly feel that the item is still worthy of the high marks and the issues are too small to demerit. Thank you, Amazon! Merry Christmas

title: DO NOT get these in bulk if the gifting is important
text: I ordered 55 gift cards for a the staff in my department at a medical facility as Christmas gifts. They were organized as 3 batches by Amazon (2 batches of 20 and one of 15) but only two of the three batches shipped, and the other was listed as delayed (when originally ordered they did not require anyone to be home to receive the shipment). I contacted customer service who assured me the third batch would arrive within 24 hours. It did not. I contacted them again and they assured me someone would get back to me to sort this our. they did not. on the third call they connected me ( after much discussion) to someone who told me there were two options: either way they would cancel the lost (on their end) cards, and I could either have the funds refunded to my credit card (with a 5-6 day lag to credit the funds) or they could apply it (over the next 4 hours) to an Amazon Gift card credited to my amazon account. I was assured by the Amazon representative that this latter refund could be applied to a reorder of the cards. What they would not do (but what would have made the most sense) was cancel and reissue the lost cards. I chose the method of applying the funds to my amazon account. HOWEVER, when I went back on line to reorder 20 cards, first I discover they now required that someone had to be home to receive the cards, AND they would not allow the funds put into my account to be used for gift cards. I again called customer service and was told I would be called back but did not hear from them and so called back again at which time I was put on the phone with a 'manager'. This gentleman confirmed that the money funded back to me could not be applied to gift cards, and that the cards could not be reissued but would have to be repurchased. All he could do was cancel the 1000$ 'card' credited to my Amazon account and send the refund to my bank card. I would then need to reorder the gift cards (with another 1000$ from my credit card), and by the way, for my trouble he wanted to give me one month of Amazon on the house (really?!). The story should have ended here, but it did not. It appears the person in customer service who put in the cancelation of the lost cards, applied that cancelation to the batch of 20 cards I actually received rather than the one that was lost, so more than half the cards I had (20+15) were now empty/cancelled. And of course I did not discover this until cards were distributed and could not be used. So I have paid for 55 cards of which at most only 35 work (not all the cards have been tried yet), and I still have not been able to reach anyone at Amazon who can make this right. Not only have I not gotten what I paid for, I have lost several hours on the phone trying to get this fixed, and people I really care about have effectively received coal in their stockings at exactly the time you want to let the folks who work for you know how much you care about them.....as I said at the beginning. Don't get this item for those you care about. And if you want good customer service, DON'T EXPECT IT FROM AMAZON!

title: DON'T PUT THIS ON YOUR REGISTRY
text: I am a loyal Amazon customer. I have been a Prime member for years and so when it was time for my (now) husband and I to make a registry for our wedding, Amazon was an obvious option. As I searched through all the options of things to put on the registry, this popped up as a suggestion. My husband and I both work multiple jobs and money is always tight, so I figured if we were given this as a gift, it would be a nice excuse to get away for a weekend. Well, it turns out if people contribute money towards this in your registry, you don't actually get the gift cards. You are just given credit to Amazon. After 1 email, 2 different people on messenger, and 4 different people on the phone I was told it is illegal to use group gifting contributions on Amazon for a gift card to something else. When I said to the man "this makes no sense, why was this Massanutten gift card even an option then?" his response was "well, your guest got a pop-up box explicitly explaining the federal laws." I could be wrong but I think most times when we see a picture of a gift card and a title saying "Massanutten Gift Card" people think it is generally straight forward. Well, it's not. text: I'm not sure if this is known or not but you can set up a gift card to be your main payment here on Amazon, set up refills with a credit card if it goes below a certain limit, have your digital rewards for shipping and stuff come to that same gift card, and skip having your credit card being a playground for price changes and rewards credit with Amazon. I do my budget and the thing that frustrates me about stores and their price changes, such as WM and Amazon, is that I already calculated in my ledger for items when they do changes. Then I have to go in and find which line it was on, what was changed, calculate the difference, and create a new line item in my ledger. It's annoying for me and I was burning through line after line every week. Enter the gift card option for Amazon and I no longer need to worry about doing that. It's kind of like a store credit except it's my money that I put on there. And the fact that the company will put the rewards from shipping delay incentives on there and such is actually brilliant. I think WM needs to follow suit with this philosophy. Obviously, keep an eye on the price changes to make sure they're not going the other way to some extent but it's way less of a headache to just let Amazon do Amazon in Amazon's gift card thing. I love this idea and I think more companies need to follow suit.

title: Extremely convenient-- apparently out of necessity
text: Amazon makes it so easy to reload gift cards, but it doesn't really make up for their horrendous gift card policy in the first place. They should have an option to just use one gift card at a time instead of lumping them all together and forcing you to use them all at once, or else use none of them at all. I suppose I can see where this might be convenient to some, but for the general population, please, make our lives a little easier and give us the option to separate out our gift cards! Almost every other website is smart enough to let people do this. Why not Amazon? Reloading my gift card balance has been the only workaround I've found to this issue so far, but at least it works like a dream. I try to keep my gift cards untouched unless I'm purchasing digital media like movies or ebooks, since it helps me set an 'internal budget' on my Amazon-sourced entertainment. This way is fast and easy and lets me (sort of) handle my gift card spending so that I can spend part or all of my balance on various purchases. Of course, the main problem still exists...but in lieu of a solution to that, this is a fairly simple way to bypass the issues it causes.

When I tried to use it by swiping it at an Applebees restaurant was informed by the machine that the "Card is Expired" -- only problem is, according to Applebee's FAQ the cards NEVER expire. So what's with this message. When attempting to enter the Card#, after getting home, on their Card checking webpage -- the card# wasn't recognized. Then, after going to the trouble to track down their customer service # and giving them a call (the 800# on the card was ONLY for checking card balances), found that the card had a $50 balance and no declined transactions. So, I guess, NOW I can return to an Applebees restaurant and have them enter the card manually into their system. And then call their customer service whenever I wish to check the balance. Safe yourself some grief -- pass on this card! Get American Express instead, more flexible and works better!

text: I have three grandkids with birthdays in April, July and September that I like to give gift cards to. But this year 2 of the three gift cards (ordered on April 6 and September 11) have not arrived on time even though they were ordered on time and with delivery dates well before the birthdays. This has resulted in upsetting my grandkids and me a lot! You should not promise to deliver simple items like gift cards if you cannot manage to deliver them on time! This is terrible service from a world-renowned company! Furthermore, when I had contacted Amazon about the delayed gift card in April, the associate I chatted with told me that they will not charge me for the gift card since it was not delivered on time and that it will be free of cost, but then Amazon proceeded to cancel the gift card! My grandchild tried using the gift card, only to find that it was cancelled and was terribly upset (understandably so)! The associate simply lied to me last time and told me that the gift card would be free of cost due to the delay! I spend a lot of money on Amazon gift cards every year, but I will be left with no choice but to stop using Amazon altogether and look for other vendors due to this abysmal service! The final straw was the gift card ordered on September 11, which Amazon says has been already fulfilled and claimed, even though they also say that it has not even been delivered (and the tracking confirms it)! I was planning to send another Amazon gift card for a substantial amount for someone else now, but given the fact that the gift card that was supposed to be delivered on Monday has still not been delivered by Thursday, I am going to have to find an alternative way. There have been no efforts whatsoever on Amazon's part to fix the problem, and empty words of apology every time I contact Amazon are just not enough to make amends for upsetting my grandkids.

title: Not a traditional gift card, but there is a solution if you have a Family Plan and want to use it
text: It is unlikely that anyone will read reviews on a gift card, but I am writing this review just in case. Amazon identifies this as a “gift card” and treats it as such for the purposes of their refund/return policy. Further, it is located in the gift card section of the site. Despite this, as other reviewers have stated, this is not a true gift card. By that, I mean that it is not simply $99.00 applicable to your account. In order to get the benefit of this card, you have to get in touch with Spotify customer service and have them assist you with a “workaround” (their term). Customer service can assist you with cancelling your account (it may be possible to do this solution yourself). You will then be able to "upgrade" to Premium and apply this card. They will then walk you through further upgrading to a Family account and you can then invite your family members again (with no loss of playlists). At that point, you will have been given "credit" for the amount and will have your next payment for the Family Plan due in about six months. However, I had to spend substantial time in Spotify’s chat (no phone number that I could find) to get to this solution. The first thing suggested by Customer Service was as follows: "What I would recommend is for you to request for a refund on your card, or gift it to a special person that hasn't had Premium with us or someone with just a regular Premium plan, or have a friend take it off your hands by purchase." An absurd suggestion in my opinion. It was only after I persistently sought other options that I was given the solution I detailed above. Some might say that it is possible that the Customer Service script is to attempt to discourage you from using this solution first before giving you satisfaction, in the hopes that some card holders will simply give up. Some reviewers were able to get a refund from Amazon, but I was not given this option.

And they acknowledged there is theft happening on their registration sites, how it is allowed to continue without being fixed is mind boggling. Every couple weeks they will send out an email asking for copies of the same documents (proof of purchase) even if you already sent them in several times prior. This is a complete failure of customer service. Suggestion: Rethink this stressful risky "gift", find a different gift card company that is more reliable for customer service. The presentation box kind of gives away what's inside. And the socks are great. They're lightweight 3-season socks, thin enough for dress shoes although they're more of a crew length than calf-length. As for whether men will wear them, men who are secure about their style will wear them when appropriate. If anything, they're a bit on the formal side; you could wear them with a dark suit and no one would know (if your pants are tailored with a proper break over the shoe) unless you deliberately flash them, and even then they're pretty tame, just colored polka dots on black. The colors are updated traditional; there's red, white, and gray among the dots, but there's also turquoise, aqua, coral, and goldenrod, with red heels and goldenrod tops. I wear men's 9-1/2 to 10-1/2 4E, and these fit fine. They washed up well, with no color running or bleeding (cold water wash, regular dry).

That wasn't a problem, because I found that Amazon would ship the gift card in a very nice gift enclosure card in only 2 days!!! I don't think there is anything more convenient than that. In this particular gift swap game, participants were allowed to "steal" co-workers' presents, and the Amazon gift card was stolen more often than anything else - it was definitely the most popular item at the party. I would recommend this gift card to anyone, but especially the person who needs a gift and doesn't know the recipient's particular shopping preferences. title: Worked 2/3 times
text: I'll be honest, I didn't expect much nor did I even know this feature existed until a few minutes ago. I mainly wanted to use old pre-paid debit cards to pay for a "splurge" purchase. I was not offered nor did I expect to receive any of the rebates/rewards that other reviewers are talking about. At first I felt a bit mischievous, like.. is this ok? Am I doing something weird that I'm not supposed to be doing, combining all these prepaid cards into one balance? And it was fine, for the first two cards, both prepaid Visa debit cards, and I was pretty happy when my email dinged and my balance was updated as expected. For the "name on card" data input I used "GIFT CARD RECIPIENT" for both and that worked out fine. One reviewer stated that the cards had to be registered prior to being used for this purpose. I registered one of them (it was a Wal-Mart branded gift card from Visa) and the other didn't have any obvious way of registering it so I didn't do anything, and both worked the same and took roughly the same amount of time to update in my account balance. Pretty cool way to use up prepaid debit cards with a miscellaneous balance, but.... The third try was not a charm, more like three strikes and I was out of luck. I tried using a prepaid AMEX, which happened to have the most value of the three cards (all were under $100), and it was declined. I read some reviews that said Amazon does an authorization check by dinging the card for $1 (Amazon's policy on prepaid cards also mentions this, it's not really a charge I guess? I'm not a finance guy so I really don't know), and tried again using $1 less than the known value of the card. Still declined. Not sure what the reason is or could be. The email explaining the decline listed some standard reasons for why it might have declined. Interestingly, one of the reasons listed in that email was that the name on the card didn't match exactly what the bank had on file... being a gift card, there was no name on the card, though it did say "a gift for you" which I listed in the "name on card" data field for the first try. Then I tried a second time and entered "GIFT CARD RECIPIENT" in the name field, which worked for the previous two cards, but no luck this time around. Not sure what's up with that, not a big deal I guess, as I said I expected nothing going into this. Obviously other reviewers have pointed out some crazy stuff that happened to them, I'd say be meticulous and pay attention to all the little details so you don't accidentally reload from your checking account when you don't mean to, but other than that my experience was positive.... 2/3 of the time. I'll make sure I update this review if I can make the third card work.

I'm disabled and I deal with a lot of pain from RA and Osteoarthritis, so my pain and subsequently, the meds I take, affect my memory. I usually try to purchase one or two gift cards when I can afford them, to have on hand for this very reason. That way, when I see my celebrating loved ones, I can always have "their present" right in the next room or in my pocket, so they know my intentions, at least. Amazon designs these cards so well, they're festive and decorative, thus there's no need to wrap them! My fave, which I gave my daughter for her bday in Nov., is a black and white polka dotted purse which has pink highlights. Another one Amazon has now is an elegant shiny black card, which would be a perfect fit for my son, my surrogate sons, my grandson and my son-in-law for their bdays in Jan., Feb., March, April and Sept. It's not much money because I don't have much to spare nowadays, but its nice to show we celebrate their birth and are glad they're here! Also, Amazon gets it here fast and you don't have to worry about anyone not liking their gift!! Everyone uses Amazon!

text: I purchased this card as a birthday gift. The recipient tried to use the card in a Subway store, but was told it had to be activated first -- quite embarrassing for him and for me. But neither he nor I had received an activation code. In fact, he said the card arrived with a message that it was "ACTIVE" in bold lettering. After contacting GiftCardMall and speaking with someone who had limited English comprehension, he was told he would have to get the activation code from me. I called them myself to explain I had never received an activation code. This rep also barely spoke English, and after I had explained the problem in detail, he actually asked me to give him the activation code. (?!) Um...that's the point here. He finally promised someone would contact me within 1 business day. When that didn't happen, I called again, and was told same thing. No one ever called. I tried e-mailing instead, and received a notice that someone would reply within 1-2 business days. Four days later, I still hadn't heard from anyone. Despite 4 phone calls and 2 e-mails to GiftCardMall, they never resolved the issue, or even bothered to call me back to tell me they couldn't resolve it. After a week of waiting and no response whatsoever, I finally insisted on speaking with a supervisor, who issued the first apology I had received for the problem but asked me to be "patient". Yeah, right. All this trouble and waiting for such a simple, basic problem. I insisted on a refund if they couldn't resolve the problem that day -- not the same old "1 to 2 business days" later routine...again. Several hours later I received a refund notice. Finally, at last, a response. GiftCardMall clearly has some serious problems in the customer service department -- not the least of which are language barriers. Their reps could sorely use some intensive customer service training and lessons on follow-through.

title: Happy to have extra $5.00 in my gift card balance.
text: As I was making a purchase thru Amazon, I was offered additional $5.00 to my gift card if I placed an order for $100.00 to my gift card balance and my remaining balance owed would be $107.00 on an item costing $112.00. I had never done this and was not aware of how it worked. I followed the blue links to read about it because I wanted to use all of my remaining gift card balance to make my purchase, not just the $5.00 being offered. I read the reviews. One review stated you can only use your gift card balance to make purchases. Another stated they never received their additional $5.00 credit after reloading their gift card. I went ahead and reloaded $100.00 on my gift card, and immediately received email that $100.00 was added to my gift card balance. I was expecting it to say $105.00 was being added. I went ahead and purchased my $112.00 item in full with my gift card balance and immediately received email notice that my additional $5.00 credit had been applied to my gift card balance. I made another purchase today for another item on Amazon with the intention to use reward points on one of my credit cards already on file as one of my payment methods. When I placed the order, the payment method had defaulted to use the remaining balance on my gift card balance. I selected the blue link to change payment method to use my reward points on my credit card with any remaining balance to be paid with my credit card and removed the black dot on the radial button for my gift card balance by clicking on it and was able to save the remaining of my gift card balance with this purchase. I reviewed everything in my order to make sure it was correct before submitting it. I am giving a 4 star review because the system had defaulted to encourage me to use my gift card balance using $5.00 with my first order and I wanted to pay in full with my gift card balance since I had just made purchase of $100.00 to reload it and also because the second purchase I made defaulted to pay with my remaining gift card balance. I had to make changes to suit me each time I placed my order. Otherwise, I am grateful to have the extra $5.00 in my gift card balance.
