title: Swiss Army Gift Card - Don't Be Fooled By Cheap Imitations
text: I really don't know why this requires a review... It's a gift card. Well, here goes anyway - They ship very fast and come in a nice little box that makes it easy to give to someone. The gift card is a magnificent flexible plastic with beautiful print on the front (design of your choosing). It looks and smells like plastic too! Not that fake plastic either. It's definitely real plastic. I had it sent to a lab to verify this. I found out that the plastic itself added some value to the card beyond what was loaded on it (fraction of a cent). It's thin and can easily be put in your wallet or purse without taking up too much space. A real treasure to own. Cons: Despite their very high quality, these don't last very long. Rarely do they last more than a couple of weeks before their value drops to zero. I've heard stories of folks who have made them last longer but they're usually people dedicated to the task with a lot of will power. This was not the case for me. Alternate Uses: Don't be fooled by the description, these cards have many uses before, during, and after their value plummets to zero. Here are a few things that I have used them for... - Applying Drywall Patch Material - Smoothing out Caulk in corners - Cracking open laptops for repair - Getting into a locked room in my house - All purpose, non abrasive scraper - Paint guard - Makeshift Ninja Throwing Star - Small protective mat for gluing things *Please note that Amazon sells products to do all these things already but they don't fit in your wallet. These things are like Swiss Army Knives, conveniently saving me time by being readily accessible. Like any knife, remember to clean it when you're done using it.

title: As of this review, cannot redeem on Vudu - and info not retained by Fandango
text: When the acquisition of Vudu by Fandango became official, I tried to purchase a Fangango gift card via Walmart.com. I like doing this because I use this method to try and budget my spending on movies. Understandably, fraud alerts are triggered because there are lots of issues with illegally purchased gift cards. However, rather than trying to contact the legit customer, the purchase attempt stays pending indefinitely. This has happened before and it’s very frustrating. After finally reaching someone at Walmart’s CS, they agreed to try processing the purchase again. I also asked for confirmation that the Fandango gift card was good for purchases thru Vudu. They said yes. The gift card purchase still never went through. I found out later that Fandango’s cards are not good on Vudu. These issues are mostly on Walmart... but that’s gripe number one. I decided to purchase a $25 gift card through a local retailer. I then went to the Fandango site to purchase movies. Once I entered the gift card info, I discarded the card - assuming the code entry would be retained... like most businesses. It is not on Fandango. After multiple communications with Fandango’s customer service, they advised that, although I redeemed a portion of my gift card for a purchase, they cannot retrieve the gift card number used. This is hard to believe, but there was nothing I could do. Essentially, the rest of my gift card balance was lost. I didn’t give a 1 star rating because it’s my fault for not keeping the gift card info after using it once. However, Fandango’s inability to retain gift card info is not only a huge inconvenience for the consumer, it results in a loss of revenue for Fandango when the customer cannot purchase more. Apparently there are Vudu gift cards out there - but I’ve yet to find them locally or on a website. I can only assume that Fandango gift cards will one day be good on Vudu - but so far, my reasonable assumptions haven’t gone too well. Until then, Fandango AND Vudu need to make it abundantly clear (on the payment entry pages and everywhere else) that Fandango’s gift cards are not valid thru Vudu.

title: A complete rip-off. Avoid like the plague.
text: I can't argue strongly enough against these things. My son got me one for my birthday, which was sweet as heck of him - and the next chance I got, we made plans to go see a movie together. When I arrived at the theater and tried to actually *use* the card, however, I found that you can't do so - the card has to be activated somehow (yet when you go to the fandango site and try to do anything along those lines, all it does is give you a list of movies). In other words, the only way, apparently, you can actually *use* the card is to order your tickets online ahead of the showing. So, if you aren't positive of which movie you're going to see before you head out, you're out of luck. Given that I don't always know precisely how long it's going to take for us to get all the way across town to the theater, this is an asinine hoop to jump through. Either we can block out an extra hour to see our movie - and sit through forty five minutes of obnoxious, inescapable TV commercials that we *pay* to endure - or I can't use the heartfelt gift my kid gave me. Poor guy spent his own money because he wanted to see a movie with his dad to celebrate my birthday, and, quite frankly, I feel like he got ripped off. If you want to give a movie-going gift, I'd suggest pretty much anything other than this. See if the theater has gift certificates. Give a pre-paid visa card. Anything. It's absurd that a gift card - which was paid for with cash - is about as convenient to use as an expired discount coupon you cut out of the back of a cereal box. UPDATE: I finally used the cards by ordering some tickets online - and had to pay a CONVENIENCE FEE ON TOP OF EVERYTHING ELSE. Yes, for the non-convenience of not even being able to USE these unless I order ahead of time, four bucks of my son's cash was just sucked into the great aether. I'll never voluntarily give Fandango a dime of my money ever again. My kid is awesome. Fandango isn't.

title: Frustrating...
text: The service does work as intended, however this evening has been has been a total unnecessary frustration because of this "reload" service. Long story short, the past couple days I researched various parts for a new computer build and finally concluded my order summary. The entire order was Prime eligible to have fast shipping, and I had been watching the Amazon purchase timer to make the indicated shipping date. Then I found out that you can't use two cards to pay for your purchase, and perhaps this is well known for frequent Amazon shoppers, but I rarely order items these days. After learning of this, I then spent the next 30 minutes looking at what options were available to get around this problem, and found at least three prominent suggestions between forums & videos. The most commonly suggested fix to this problem was to use the account "reload" option and within 5-10 minutes you could pay the specified partial amount towards the order using the loaded "Gift Card" balance. Well two hours later it posts, and of coarse the shipping time is not eligible. Given that I'm going to be working, I can't have an order as important at this delivered when no one is home. UPS, Fedex, and USPS have all left packages sitting by the gates of my home, and of coarse things have been stolen (Multiple Houses) UPS is the only service which has noted the problem and now mandated their drivers to go to the actual door after I spoke up about to them. I had arranged for someone to be home on delivery day which worked out well for them as well, but with the delay now in shipping it won't work. I rarely ever complain about things, but this type of scenario should of been resolved years ago. The solution should be clearly stated on the check out screen, and the alternative option convenient for the customer. I mean seriously, when your the customer spending a large amount of money, you shouldn't have to go run around looking for solutions that may or may not work. If I had known it would of taken 2 hours to use the balance, I would just done two orders, which has worked just fine in the past but requires more time to do but hell I would made the deadline. Anyways I hope no one else makes my mistake. Fry's Electronics had 80% of the items at the same price in store, with two items slightly cheaper, and 1 item $20 more. If you have one or have something similar, it's can be worth while to just check them out. The tax may be a little more which is what discouraged me, but you can use TWO payments, holy hell... out the door and back home for just a little more effort and $$. Anyways, I just hope there is no more issues going forwards. Don't get me wrong, I'm still gonna use Amazon in the future, but just for small stuff going forwards.

title: Took hours to reload balance
text: More than anything else, convenience is what Amazon sells to the world. So convenience is what we expect and grow accustomed to. When Amazon is not convenient it is extremely frustrating. So my son had a couple of $100.00 visa gift cards and really wanted to purchase an IPOD. I tried using them to help make the purchase, but once I entered one of the cards to make the purchase, it took my order without telling me to enter another source for additional funds. Realizing that Amazon would have to cancel the transaction because it only allowed for one payment source, I cancelled the transaction and tried to enter the Visa gift cards onto an Amazon.com gift card so that I could then add them together to make the purchase. So I first added the amount over $200.00 that I would need to make the purchase to my Amazon.com gift card then and tried to enter the Visa gift cards. Amazon would not accept the gift cards. Since I already had the extra money on an Amazon.com gift card, I decided to "buy" my son's visa gift cards to use elsewhere and put $200.00 onto Amazon.com gift card from my own funds. The transaction appeared as pending for hours. After a while, I gave up waiting and just paid for my son's purchase. Now I have $200.00 on an Amazon.com gift card that I will likely eventually use, but never really wanted there in the first place. I suppose there is a way to reverse the charge, but everything related to the Amazon.com gift seems to be so complicated, I just don't want to take the time and hassle to do it. I probably don't even have the time to write this review, but I am so annoyed by how long it took to accomplish this transaction. If Amazon is going to continue to make a run on leading the retail world, it will have to figure out how people can make purchases with visa gift cards. It will also have to figure out how to reload balances without making customers wait hours. If it continues to be this complicated, some other retailer will figure out how to do it, and shoppers will go elsewhere.

But buying a gift card to Subway, in what I can only assume is some passive aggressive plea for attention is not an appropriate way of dealing with your feelings. Do you really think that tricking innocent people into eating soggy vegetables, dry meats and anything but fresh condiments is going to help? title: Excellent value! But "Gift note" is misleading...
text: This is an awesome deal. I remember years ago I tried searching for Amazon gift cards on Amazon, and I couldn't find anything, other than gift "cards" that you could purchase, and then the recipient would receive an email only - no physical goods to speak of. And you know what? In my opinion, that sucks. Ya, there doesn't *need* to be a physical card, but when I give a gift, I'd like to be able to *give* that person something tangible. Enter: The Amazon.com Gift Card. So, it's great that they offer a number of different designs at a number of different price points. One caveat: on the Amazon Mobile App on Android, it can be confusing as to how to choose the denomination and card design that you want. This is best purchased from the regular website. I got 3 different gift cards on here, each $20. Each arrived as promised. And why do I say these are a great value? Free 1 or 2 day shipping. AND, you get the gift card at no charge. In my opinion, the art on these cards are classy, and they're not printed on cheap paperstock either. So, why didn't I give this 5 stars? I think Amazon could be a little clearer that adding a "Gift Note" to your order doesn't get the message printed on the greeting card. The greeting card arrives to you inside of a plastic mailing envelope, with the gift card mounted in the greeting card, and an envelope. The package is more suited for it to be delivered to *you*, and then you write your note, and then mail or hand it off to your recipient. I think I read some other reviews from people saying that they ordered these to deliver straight to their recipient, and the person received the aforementioned package. Oh, and if you order add a Gift Note during checkout, it prints on bottom of the packing slip... Not exactly ideal presentation, when there's a brand new greeting card and envelope in the same shipping sleeve... [Update] I see they've since updated the description to mention the above "Gift Note" issue, and how exactly it is packaged.... Way to go, Amazon! This has been changed from 4 to 5 stars.

The bad news: The website allows you to enter text for the greeting card, and even reminds you to enter the names of the recipient and sender. I entered the text, but omitted the names of the recipients and my name because I was ordering them in bulk, and wanted to personally sign the card. First surprise was that when the cards arrived, they were in individual SEALED envelopes, so I couldn't sign the card. I later found out from the recipients that the text I submitted to be included in the greeting card was completely omitted. So, if you want to personalize the card, it may be best to use the option to print the card yourself.

title: Kindle gift card only works for Kindle-related purchases.
text: All I asked for this Christmas was Amazon gift cards. So a relative went to Best Buy to ask for one, and she was handed an Amazon Kindle Gift Card. I wasn't sure if this would work for general Amazon purchases, so I sent an e-mail to Amazon customer service. The reply I received from Amazon was that the Kindle Gift Card can only be used for Kindle-related purchases, NOT for Amazon general merchandise. I tried to take the card back to Best Buy to exchange it for a regular Amazon gift card (which is what she asked for from the sales associate, so apparently, even retailers are unaware of this policy, although when I returned the manager knew this probably because others were trying to return their Kindle gift cards). Anyway, the manager there said it cannot be returned or exchanged, and confirmed it can only be used to make Kindle-related purchases. He said this is an Amazon return policy, not a Best Buy policy. Now the real question is, why would anyone in their right mind want an Amazon Kindle Gift Card with all these limitations, when they could get a regular Amazon gift card and buy anything at the Amazon store, including Kindle related purchases. This is a ridiculous policy, and if anyone says I'm lying, I'll be happy to forward the e-mail I received from Amazon customer service concerning this issue. *** UPDATE: Someone from Amazon called me to say if I first put the Amazon Kindle Gift Cards into my account using the number before making a purchase the money should be available for other purchases. They also sent me an e-mail with more specific instructions. Not sure if this is a rule change or what, but I appreciate them taking the time out to call me and leave another e-mail. I'll post the new e-mail below with the instructions (the first e-mail telling me it cannot be used this way is in the comments discussion to this review). Kudos to Amazon for listening to their customers if this is true (And I assume it is). I have not used the cards yet, and hadn't even scratched the off the cover over the numbers because I was thinking about trying to have Amazon exchange them for regular Amazon gift cards. Anyway, I'll bump up my rating to 3 stars (minus 2 for the misinformation) and the new e-mail is below: Hello Bill, I'm sorry for the misinformation you have previously received in an email from us about using your Gift Card for purchases on Amazon.com. I've tried contacting you at the phone number listed in your Amazon.com account but have been unsuccessful. To use an Amazon.com Gift Card (or a Gift Card with the Kindle name on it) for purchases from Amazon.com, visit Your Account (http://www.amazon.com/your-account) and look for the gift card option in the Payments section. You can also enter your gift card claim code during checkout in the box labeled "Have any gift cards, gift certificates or promotional claim codes?" in the right column. If you use 1-Click ordering, you'll find a similar option if you click "Review or edit your 1-Click orders" after clicking "Buy now with 1-Click" on a product's page. You'll find more instructions here: http://www.amazon.com/help/giftcards If you still need help, you can contact us via phone, chat, or e-mail by clicking the "Contact Us" button on any Help page (http://www.amazon.com/help). I hope this helps! We look forward to seeing you again soon. Megan

text: Amazon blocked the option to submit a review for the actual gift card so I have to pay this here... Bait & Switch by Amazon: Get a $10 credit when you send a $50 Amazon Gift Card by text message Reviewed in the United States on October 10, 2017 Subject: Get a $10 credit when you send a $50 Amazon Gift Card by text message If you received that promotion email from Amazon, be very careful. My purchase experience with that promotion felt like a "bait & switch" by Amazon website. I clicked on the promotion email link and tried to buy a $50 gift card. I entered the phone number for texting the gift card and as I clicked "Buy Now" button, Amazon website reloaded the gift-card purchase page & prompted me to enter an email address because the delivery option was changed (by Amazon) to "Deliver by Email". I was confused and tried it to start over two more times. Both times, after I entered a phone number where the gift card would be delivered to, and clicked on "Buy Now" button, Amazon website would reload the page and change to "Deliver by Email". Somewhat out of patience, I just proceeded to enter an email and completed the whole purchase. After reading the fine print of this promotion, I realized that $10 credit is given only when the $50 gift card is delivered by text to a phone number. To me, the whole experience is a "bait & switch". I wanted to buy $50 gift card and I followed the email link & entered a phone number. As I wanted to pay for the purchase, Amazon website changed the delivery option to "Deliver by Email" to mislead me into entering an email address to deliver the gift card. In turn, that would disqualify me for the $10 credit.

It's made of thick, high quality card stock and should hold up to the tugging of almost any child - in fact, you could probably reuse it a number of times. There's plenty of space on the back to write a message, so there's no need to spend money on a separate greeting card. The card also has no branding, so you can replace the Amazon gift card with some other gift card if you wish. The cartoon chicken and the bright colors will appeal to young children, but it's also mature & simplistic enough to be appropriate for a teen or adult. I was very impressed by the quality of an item that is essentially free, and I definitely recommend this for an Easter present or any egg-related holiday. The item came completely undamaged in a sealed plastic cover and was well protected during shipping, but YMMV. Sometimes Amazon's gift card tins arrive dented and scratched, and other times they're in perfect condition - it all depends on the person who packages and handles it.

title: Check your payment preferences before adding funds
text: Word to the wise! Amazon will charge other payment forms without your explicit consent or even notification of your original payment fails. TURN OFF THAT SETTING IF YOU WANT TO AVOID A HEADACHE. (Account, payment preferences, scroll all the way to the bottom and click “backup payment preferences,” toggle option off). We didn’t realize Amazon charged other cards instead of loading those visa gift cards to the balance. Here’s the quick and dirty: -I had one of those visa gift cards from a rebate. -I had a purchase I washed to make on Amazon. -The purchase was for more than my visa gift card. -Amazon doesn’t allow you to specify multiple forms of payment at checkout. -I “loaded” my visa gift card to my amazon balance. -I received an e-mail three days later showing my $50 was added. -I made my purchase. -Weeks later, I noticed a $50 charge on a different credit card. I called, was told to dispute the charge with my credit card company. It was ultimately denied. So, that visa rebate gift card was never loaded to the account. -Some time later, we learned that there’s a place where you can turn off a setting, one that I was never told about, that will charge another card of your first payment method doesn’t process.

The majority of the background colors of the packaging I received were green while four of backgrounds were red. The chocolate is made with milk chocolate (sugar, cocoa butter, whole milk, chocolate, soy lecithin, and PGPR (emulsifiers), and vanilla. The product contains milk and soy. The manufacturer noted that it was manufactured on equipment which processes wheat, peanut butter, and almonds. If you have an allergy to one or all of these food products, please be aware. The best by date for the product that I received is 9 months from the date that I received it. The product was Manufactured in the USA (Reading, PA). Am I alone in this category of consumers?? I can see how someone who's distracted (or maybe elderly) can accidentally use their credit card or bank account to reload their balance instead of an intended gift card. text: I recently gifted this to a family member for Christmas, and was very pleased with the delivery. Here's why to get this: 1. It saved me the hassle of gift wrapping it. Don't bother with the 'gift wrap' option during checkout either. The box is elegantly wrapped as it is. 3. It came in a large envelope rather than a full blown Amazon box, so the family member really didn't have a clue as to what it was until she opened her box. 4. The variety of gift card designs that you can pick from that can be boxed gives you the flexibility to choose the right card for your occassion. 5. My gift recipient is a huge Kindle fan. With the gift card, she got herself some books that she enjoyed rather than some odd gift I might have picked. She also shopped for some other stuff on Amazon that she would not have otherwise. So needless to say, this gift worked well for her. If you were gifting this to someone in person rather than having it delivered, then you may want to get a small greeting card to place inside the box as an identifier. There is no place to note your name or greetings on the box itself. This isn't a fault. It's what you expect from a great gift box.

text: I purchased this $50 Apple Gift card on Prime Day at the sale price of $40.00. Once I received it, I pealed off the strip to reveal the redemption code. The card must have been old or stored in the heat as the peal removed most of the first three characters of the redemption code.I could not read it. Apples redemption scanner couldn't read it either. What do you do with a card that you can not redeem? I decided to try Apple support. They require you to email them along with images of both sides of the card and my receipt. Simple enough? Nope. Safari on my Mac would not let me attach it to the email as required. I then redid the email on an iPad, re-took the images and successfully added the card images. But not the Amazon receipt. It would not accept a pdf or image of the receipt. I ended up taking a screen print of the receipt. That worked. Now I must wait on the generosity of Apple to provide a new card. If they refuse, I'm out $40. Clearly either Apple had a bad print on the card or Amazon did not store it properly and the strip adhesive was damaged. The card does look and feel "old" but can't swear to it. The moral of the story is don't buy gift cards. Once you give up your money for them, you have no real recourse if the card can't be redeemed. Buyer beware.

I was attempting to (at least slightly) personalize this gift but ended up feeling like I'd just left a warehouse store with a bulk purchase of gift cards...which is exactly what I'll do next time; at least then I'll know what to expect. NEVER AGAIN!

title: DO NOT BUY AMAZON GIFT CARDS - NO SOLUTION TO STOLEN CODES AND ZERO BALANCE
text: My Amazon Gift Card arrived with the claim code already revealed. It had no balance on it. Amazon said they can't replace the card or refund my money. I have been purchasing Amazon gift cards for years. I like the boxes and tins they provide. Sadly, I recently found out from friends that sometimes the gift cards I had been gifting had $0 on them but they felt bad telling me. Being that it was much later, I could no longer do anything about it. However, it happened again…this December 2022, I purchased a $50 Amazon gift card. The claim code was already revealed (it didn't have the orange strip covering it). I called Amazon and they said the card was not valid and they would refund my money. They didn't refund my money, so I had to call back again. This time they said they couldn't refund my money because the gift card was canceled. They weren’t sure what to do next, so they escalated the issue and told me to wait 24 hours. I received an email from the escalation team that said, "I've researched your Amazon Gift Card and found it is unable to use. I tried to issue refund however I'm not able to resend the gift card or refund the order. Under these circumstances, if the gift card was purchased using a credit/debit card, we suggest that the purchaser contact their bank to see what options may be available." Per Amazon’s Customer Service’s instructions, I disputed the charge with my credit card company. A few hours later I received an angry email from Amazon telling me that I disputed a charge and they would still need to receive payment from me for the disputed charge so they will be charging my credit card on file. Now I’m getting charged twice for something I never received! I can't believe a company like Amazon would do this! It's fraudulent to keep issuing gift cards with no money and then insisting on charging customers for the missing funds. To top it all off, they had the nerve to sign off on their email saying they are building the “Earth's Most Customer-Centric Company.” NEVER BUY THESE GIFT CARDS! IMPOSSIBLE TO GET YOUR MONEY BACK.

Approximately one hour later I received an e-mail from Amazon stating that I needed to change my account password with no real reason given. I went on the Amazon website and did so. After this, I discovered that Amazon's computer system for whatever reason did not properly charge my credit card so the transaction must have been flagged as potential fraud. I changed my password and successfully added the $50 to my gift card. Today I decided to add more money to the gift card and now, one hour later, there is still a delay. I have the feeling that again there will be a problem and I'll have to change my Amazon password. Word to the wise, don't try to add funds to your gift card because Amazon's computer system treats that as a security breach.

title: Buyer beware
text: The one-day shipping is great but please read the fine print first. I ordered a gift card for my sister and her husband. They were on vacation so I had it shipped to their post office box rather than their home. While the terms of one-day shipping prohibit this, when I placed my order there was no alert at check-out, otherwise I would have had it shipped to me and mailed it myself. The card was delivered by UPS and simply set on their porch for anyone to see and steal or be blown away by the wind. I had to drive to their home, retrieve the card, and mail it myself as they were gone for another six days. The problem is that Amazon had the post office box address on the label; UPS changed the delivery address to their home which is totally irresponsible. The irony is that I even provided my phone number on check-out after being prompted; UPS never called me. While I should have read the fine print first, I also feel that Amazon should have had some way of preventing me from entering a post office box number on the shipping address. Furthermore, it was completely inexcusable for UPS to change the address especially without calling me first.

title: I tried to use a visa gift card to reload ...
text: I tried to use a visa gift card to reload my Amazon.com gift balance. The visa gift card had a balance of exactly $100. If you ordered a $100 amazon gift card you got an extra 5-10 dollars. Plan was to use the visa card to buy an amazon card and get the extra money. 1st try the card was rejected. No reason. I thought it was because it was a visa gift card so I spent a considerable amount of time trying to figure out if there was something wrong with my card. Tried again. 2nd try was also rejected. These aren't instant rejections.... they are card denied rejections that happen 5-10 minutes after the order happens. Again no reason as to why this happened. Called customer service. The advice there wasn't helpful and they didn't really know what was going on. What I eventually figured out was that each time I put an order in, it was charging a $1 authorisation fee to the card. Then the card has a $99 balance instead of $100 and the transaction is rejected. Probably not news to most people but its not common knowledge, after all Amazon Customer Service didn't know what was up...

She did agree and comment on how nice the Santa display was, but insisted on suggesting other alternatives. title: Company Gift Card Fraud
text: Amazon gift cards are the biggest fraud I have ever seen! My husband was issued a $50 gift card from his work over a year ago and had been waiting to use it on something he or I needed. With Christmas just around the corner he and I thought it would be a great idea to use the gift card to buy gifts with. My husband spent $24 dollars and change leaving me a balance of $25 dollars to use if I wanted to buy something. I thought hey this is perfect! I can buy my nephew the movie he asked for and a few other small items for stockings and not break the bank. Well of course life doesn't work out the way it is supposed to. Because my husband and I each have our own Amazon accounts, created before we were married, and maintained for buying the surprise birthday, Christmas, or anniversary gift. And here is where the CATCH comes in... Any purchases or that were made on an Amazon gift card, or if a gift card was even just registered under a particular individual/account can not be used or shared by someone else. The powers that be at Amazon consider that transferring. This includes any minor children that may have an account not just your spouse. Which means...I would have to spend personal money out of pocket if I wanted to still buy these items off Amazon, instead of using a perfectly good gift card that would have covered the balance. Or the other option which was never suggested was log into my husbands account not look at what he bought me in his previous purchase section and buy what I wanted for my nephew and kids on my husbands account only after I ask him for his password (which he would have given me.) Don't bother taking into account that minors can not own items so to restrict the transfer of property (from parent to child) is illegal and minors can not be bound to such agreements ...and I myself live in a joint property state so at the end of the day what is my husbands is mine and mine is his.

title: Does Anyone Else Feel Like They've Been ROBBED By Amazon???
text: I purchased six $50 Amazon Gift Cards from a local supermarket (Bi Lo) to give as Christmas Gifts in 2015 (something I've done for many years). My Sister-in-law, the recipient of one of those $50 Amazon Gift Cards called me to say that she's lost the Gift Card (most likely accidentally discarded with all of the Christmas paper, etc. and burned in the trash). I told her "no problem", since I had kept my receipt from Bi Lo that includes the Amazon Gift Card Number, and I felt certain that Amazon would be able to see that no purchases had been made against their Gift Card Number and that either Amazon or Bi Lo would be able to cancel that card and issue a new one, or Credit her online Amazon Account $50 and bypass issuing a new physical card altogether. I was sadly mistaken.... when she initially contacted Amazon, they told her that since the Amazon Card was purchased from Bi Lo, we would need to take the matter up with them. I went to Bi Lo and was told that there wasn't anything that they could do and that I would need to contact Amazon. Since my Sister-in-law had already contacted Amazon and been turned away, I decided since I was the one who made the purchase and had the receipt, I would call my Credit Card Company first to see if they might be able to offer some assistance in getting the matter resolved since I had purchased all of the Gift Cards with my Credit Card. After 30 minutes discussing the details with my Credit Card Company, they said they understood my dilemma but weren't able to dispute the charge with Bi Lo. They suggested I contact Amazon directly since I had my receipt with Amazon's Gift Card number on and since it was Amazon's gift card. So... after about 30 minutes on the phone with a very nice gentleman from Amazon who made 2 attempts to get his Supervisor to approve some type of credit for the loss, he sadly informed me that Amazon isn't responsible for purchases of their Gift Cards that aren't made from their website. I told him that since Amazon isn't willing to offer any assistance, even though they can clearly see in their system a $50 unused Credit on that lost Gift Card and since I had my receipt with their Gift Card number printed on the receipt (proof that I had purchased their Gift Card), I felt as though Amazon had ROBBED me of $50, since the only one who will benefit financially from this gift transaction is Amazon and I had certainly not intended to add "Amazon" as one of my 2015 Christmas names to buy for! Furthermore, I told him that I would not be making any more purchases from Amazon directly or purchasing any other Amazon Gift Cards in the future and would encourage others to do the same. I try not to support businesses that engage in thievery, and that is exactly how I feel I was treated in this instance.

title: ... many of the reviews here in an attempt to better understand how Spa Finder works
text: I read many of the reviews here in an attempt to better understand how Spa Finder works. I did this because when trying to redeem my Spa Finder gift cards that my mom sent me for my birthday, my spa did not have a clear policy on what I could use them for and gave me a confusing explanation of how I could not use the gift card for discounted packages because I had received a discount when purchasing the gift card. First, my mom paid full price for the gift cards, so there was no discount. I had a long conversation with the owner and did some of my own research. What I learned is that Spa Finder makes money by charging a commission to the spa on the redemption of cards. In essence, Spa Finder only reimburses the spa for a percentage of the card. There is no discount to the client in purchasing the card, so spas should be aware that just because Spa Finder does not reimburse them in full for the gift cards does not mean that client received a discount (it's not a coupon or a voucher). Many of the reviews have advised to either just give the person money or a gift card directly from the spa to avoid these hassles. I have a different take on this. My mom lives across the country and she gave me these gift cards because it is more personal than sending a check or cash, and it ensures that I will use it for its intended purpose.She could not buy a card directly from the spa because of her location. Whatever you think of Spa Finder as a company, spas choose to participate in the Spa Finder program as a way of building their clientele. It is a legitimate business decision, and the price is the monthly fee the spas pay as well as the commissions on each card that is redeemed at their location. While the fees may be higher, this is a similar concept to the charges that credit card companies place on each transaction. Regardless of the transaction charges, business accept credit cards as convenience to customers so they can build their customer base. Similarly, spas participate in the Spa Finder program to build their clientele. The Spa Finder program is not mandatory, and spas know about the charges before they sign up. I do not feel sorry for spas that choose to participate in this program, so talk of "supporting" your local spa falls on deaf ears with me. A spa is not a charity that needs my support. It is a business just like any other, and I expect the spas listed on the website to accept the cards as payment. If the cost of participating in the Spa Finder program outweighs the benefits, they should not participate. Similarly, it they no longer wish to participate, they should remove their name from the Spa Finder website and place a notice on their own website that they no longer participate in the program. Spas should really think about how participating in the program will affect their business rather than leaving it up to the client to wade through the technicalities. I recommended to the owner of my spa that they add a section to their policy page explaining that because of the commissions they pay on the Spa Finder cards, clients can redeem the cards only for full-priced services and cannot apply the cards to discounted packages. Spas can develop any policy that serves their business best, but whatever the policy, it should be clearly stated to the client upfront. I gave this three stars because that means that its OK. Not great, not bad, but OK. I think it could be great, but there are obviously some things to be worked out on Spa Finder's part (based on other reviews) as well as that of businesses participating in the program. Right now, the potential loser in this situation is the client.

title: These gift cards need better branding titles
text: This Reload works fine throughout Amazon online store. Amazon Reload is what Amazon Gift/e-gift card is except Reload works only with your account. Reload or gift cards work as store credits for your Amazon Balance, can't be used as a backup payment method, nor do they work with Amazon Pay, which is another way of paying through your Amazon account to merchants outside of Amazon. However, Amazon.com Store card, which is a physical card can be used with Amazon Pay, AWS, and the rest of Amazon. Not to be confused with Amazon Rewards Visa Signature Card, which is provided by Chase, and can be used with everything I believe. Another type of physical cards are the Amazon Classic gift card, which you can find at other stores, which are the same as eGift card/Reload. Some of the cards I mentioned offer cashbacks, and do not include Amazon Business American Express cards which you might have guessed is for businesses. But a customer without a business can acquire them too for their "business needs," as stated by their FAQ, as if the other non-business cards are meant for non-business needs. There are also Kindle cards which only work with Amazon Kindle store. Here endeth the lesson of many Amazon cards.

text: I DO NOT RECOMMEND YOU CHOOSE "ONE DAY" SHIPPING if you want your gift cards to arrive in just a few days. [[ASIN:B005S28ZES Amazon.com Gift Cards - In a Gift Box - Free One-Day Shipping]]I ordered three gift cards on December 26,2011 and they shipped January 22, 2012 (so they arrived about a month after I ordered them). I understand that this was just after the holidays and maybe there was mayhem in their warehouse. But common Amazon, almost a month to ship 3 gift cards? Oh, and what was supposed to be a surprise, ended up not being one at all; because after about three weeks of wondering if my family members received these items, I finally started asking. So not only did I ruin the surprise, but also found out that after 3 weeks of placing the order, no one had received anything. On the 22nd of January I received an email saying my order had just shipped, with no apology. Amazon should program their system to send an apology email, if an order takes way too long to ship. And, I really think they need to stop advertising 1 day shipping, if they can't get the job done in 1 day.

title: Hugely Disappointing Gift
text: Hugely disappointing gift. I'm not a big fan of gift cards in general, but I have received Amazon cards in the past. Amazon has a huge selection of items to purchase, great prices, and there were no problems activating and using my card - so that's fine. ... but that was Amazon, and Staples is not Amazon. By way of comparison, the Staples gift card has been a huge disappointment. First, there is NO VALUE PRINTED ON THE CARD, so you have to go check the balance to even know what you have. Then when I went to the Staples website to check the cards balance, it kept telling me that the card number was invalid (though I verified both the card number and PIN were correctly entered several times, and even tried it a second and third time from another computer with a different browser). I was beginning to think I had a counterfeit card, but decided to re-check the card using the Staples 888 phone number, and that did work, so the card was fine. So the first disappointment was that Staples wasted over an hour of my time just trying to get the card to validate on the Staples website, only to find that the Staples website was screwed up for some reason, though the card was fine. The Staples phone verification system reported that my card is a valid $25 giftcard, but once I was finally able to verify the cards balance using the phone system, I was in for another HUGE disappointment, because prices at Staples are so horrible that, even after checking my local Staples "Weekly Ad" Sales and applying my "Gift Card" I found that in most cases, I might as well just buy the item on Amazon. In fact, in some cases the prices were so bad that I would have actually saved money to throw my gift card in the garbage and just pay Amazon's full price (because Amazon's everyday price was more than $25 dollars less). The good thing about a gift card is that the person who receives the card has 'mad money' that they can use to pick out whatever gift they want, the BAD thing is that if you give them a gift card to a store with LOUSY PRICES, then they may feel like their windfall gift money is being spent foolishly and feel bad (which pretty much sums up my feelings dealing with Staples). Also, all my past experiences with Staples have seemed to involve that old-school bait-and-switch sales model where they dangle a sale item in your face, just to try to get you into the store, then RIP YOU OFF by telling you "So sorry, the sale item you want isn't available, but we do have a fine selection of our outrageously overpriced non-sale items, so wouldn't you rather have one of those instead?" Staples is not as bad as Best Buy (who are the worst scum in the universe in regard to bait-and-switch B.S.) but after buying on Amazon for the last few years, I am not ancious to play ANY of the brick an mortar store games of scampering around town like a rat in a maze trying to find that 'deal' before it disapears. On Amazon, prices may change over time, but if an item is listed as available for a certain price, then you can buy it at the price shown, period, end of story.

I have checked all my other accounts for unauthorized activity and run several virus and malware scans and found nothing out of the ordinary except this charge. I called Amazon to see if anyone else called or emailed in the recent past requesting changes to the account. The last activity they have recorded is my own. title: Great card until
text: I have bought several of these gift cards for personal use. One of the reasons I buy these is because you can use them at stores that do not accept credit cards. You can assign a pin and use the card as a debit card. There is a grocery store that I like to shop at that will not accept credit cards but does accept visa debit gift cards such as this one. Again I think this is my 3rd or 4th card purchased from Amazon and up until this point I had no issues with this card. So what happened? There is a lot of fraud that happens with gift cards. They can be easily compromised. The gift card I purchased prior to this one did have a fraudulent charge on it. I caught it a few hours after it happened and called Paypal. They were able to stop the transaction and get me my money back. Understanding this, when I made any transactions with this card I made sure the card was not handed over to anyone. In early November I decided to check on my balance. The card was compromised. The last transaction was identical to the fraudulent charge mentioned above. A paypal charge leaving a few pennies left in the card. This gift card DOES have a way to dispute fraudulent charges. I downloaded the forms filled them out and e-mailed them to the e-mail address listed. A week later after receiving no response I sent another email inquiring on the status of my dispute. They e-mailed stating I need to send them the dispute form. I replied with the dispute form and explained I had sent it with my first e-mail. A week later no response. I sent it again to both emails asking for a status. Again no response. At this point it feels the ignorance is intentional. So here's my suggestion. Unless you use all the funds on this card within a month after purchasing it I don't recommend this card.

Whether it's purchasing household essentials, electronics, or even treating myself to a well-deserved indulgence, the extra credits from Reload provide a welcome boost to my purchasing power. Overall, Amazon Reload has become an indispensable tool in my online shopping arsenal. Its user-friendly interface, seamless integration with my bank account, and the added reward system make it a top choice for managing my Amazon spending. Honestly, it's a gift card--why would it take a week to get there? There was no inclement weather or any other reason for the delay. This is the last time I will order a gift card here. title: Southwest website gift card policy
text: Gift card came relatively quickly and was easy to use. Be aware, Southwest.com only allows you to use 3 total forms of payment per transaction. Which means if you are intending to pay entirely with gift cards, and three gift cards don't add up to the total balance of your purchase, you are only allowed to use 2 gift cards plus a 1 credit card (3 total forms) to cover the entirety of the purchase. If you try to checkout and enter three gift cards that do not cover the entirety of the purchase the system automatically removes one of the cards to give you the ability to enter a form that covers the remaining balance as the final 3rd form of payment. Given that you are only able to buy a maximum of $200 card denominations on this website, the maximum ticket price you can buy via these gift cards is $600. Long story short, if you intend to buy these gift cards on Amazon, buy the largest denominations you can to make your life easier, and plan on paying some out of pocket if you can't cover the ticket price with $600 ($200/card x 3 cards). Also, there is no way (on the website or on the phone with Southwest customer service) to combine the balance of any gift cards.

In support chat with Spotify, the problem was revealed to be associated with account bundles -- I previously had a student account that came with Hulu and Showtime. When my student account ran out (3 year max term), my access to these services terminated but they were still linked to my account, even though I had been paying the standard premium rate without Hulu/Showtime. The card could not be applied to my account with this bundle still linked to my account, support said. Spotify cancelled my premium and reverted the account to "Free." At that point the card applied to my account no problem (full 12 months). Do note that support confirmed that only 18 months may be active on your account, so if you try to redeem 2 of these cards, you will have to wait 6 months - 1 year to apply. title: I write to recommend these gift cards as a handsome addition to anyone’s ...
text: I write to recommend these gift cards as a handsome addition to anyone’s pockets. I have purchased them for family members, for friends, for inamorata, and for myself, so that when I’m strolling through the mall, or out busily driving to and fro in my car, I’ll stop and think: THE OLIVE GARDEN. I would no doubt think of it anyway, because once you have experienced their food, there’s no going back to anything lesser (CHILIS). Their alfredo sauce will almost make your mouth stagger off your face in delight. The last time I was there, I asked SCOTT the waiter for more breadsticks, and he promptly brought them. I asked him if he thought ZITI was a strange name for a food, and he said he’d never thought about it before. It sounds like a noise an animal makes, I said. Just because it sounds funny, SCOTT explained, doesn’t mean it doesn't taste good. SCOTT, I said, that is very true. Then we both leaned back and enjoyed a laugh. Someone should give SCOTT a promotion. I would offer one complaint about this fine restaurant, which is that they are fairly inflexible about letting you customize your dining experience. I know a local singer-songwriter, IVAN MALESKY, M.D, and a few months ago, I tried to hire him to serenade my table at the local OG. He is perhaps best known for the song “My Neighbor's Shoes,” a marvelous, uplifting song about fellowship and brotherhood. It was followed by the sequels “Neighbor's Pants,” “Neighbor’s Robe,” and “Neighbor's Wife,” a series that becomes increasingly vehement and artistically challenging. But I assured the OLIVE GARDEN he would express only mainstream emotions during his time in their fine establishment. No response. I wrote again to assure them that the man is extremely low-maintenance. He brings his own stepladder and has a surprisingly easygoing demeanor. He would touch their patrons in a metaphorical way ONLY, with a profound basso mysterioso that shivers the heart strings to the timeless frequencies of human longing. His actual hands he would keep to himself. I imagined he would run through his repertoire of popular standards and then do some hingeless jazz soloing when the food arrived. He would of course ask for tips, I cautioned, or have his assistant BON waddle around with a hat. But this gives the performance a classic, outdoor feel, and allows IVAN to finance his disparate endeavors. No response. I admit at this point getting a little bit gravely disappointed in the OLIVE GARDEN. It seemed inexplicable to me that my favorite restaurant would refuse to EVEN ANSWER a loyal patron after so many unbroken of friendship and what they call HOSPITALIANO. I thought back over all those meals I’ve had, and all those times I plunked five or six new gift card on the table at once, as if to say “let’s make something happen.” So in a fit of what might be called FRUSTRANGINI, I did something that, I must confess, I am not proud of. It is hard for me to admit, but in the interests of full disclosure, I will say it. I went to BENNIGANS. Perhaps six times. It was not the same. It’s not that the food is bad at BENNIGANS – one time I had the lemonish salad with chicken fragments over spicey spice. But it just lacks that special something. You just don’t feel like you’re being swept away to a faraway place, as you do in the OLIVE GARDEN. I think that’s why I enjoy the GIFT CARDS so much, for they add to the fantasy of being outside the usual parameters of time and space. Also I did not have the same kind of jokey rapport with the waitstaff at BENNIGANS. This is not a knock on BRITTNEY, KAYLA, JOSH, RICKI or LINBEE who were all very prompt and competent (except JOSH), but they did not have the expertise that you find with a SCOTT. Also my water had something floating in it. I don’t think it was a flea, but I also don’t think it was something a patron wants to have to try to block with his lips while he tries to enjoy his water. This experience made me realize that the OLIVE GARDEN is more than just food served on plates by waiters for money: there’s an idea there. It’s an idea about returning to a simpler time and a simpler place that echoes deep within the bowels of the human heart. You can see why they are the world’s most successful horizontally distributed multinational restaurant conglomeration. OG finally did respond to my questions, with a firm but polite NO. It didn’t matter, because the special event had come and gone, and MALESKY had stopped doing restaurant work to focus his energy on studio recording and his various ongoing lawsuits. Despite this disappointment, I did return. Indeed, I have decided to put aside our differences, and continue to enjoy an exhilarating, food-based relationship with the OG. There’s just something about the place that makes it impossible to stay away for long. Also, I had four gift cards left. But in this way, reader, we come full circle to the true value of the gift card. Sometimes, it forces you to eat at OLIVE GARDEN when you really don’t want to. But you’ll always be glad you did.

I chatted with an agent and was assured that redeeming Amazon gift cards online does not count as reloading, so I went ahead with my first reload. title: Uploading $600 using my credit card to my account requires verification I wasn’t aware about.
text: Sent a $600 gift card to my account to be made for future purchases using my credit card. The transaction on the surface appeared seamless, received an automated email thanking me and informing me that I should see the new/updated account balance within five minutes. That didn’t happen, instead about an hr later I get a call from a Seattle Washington number. Not knowing who it was, but suspecting it may be Amazon I just let my phone buzz. I really do not like answering my phone when I don’t know who or what is on the other end. Anyway I was left a message that was all but beyond recognizable, the only word I understood was “amazon”. Tried calling back, but of course amazon uses a random phone number generator, so all I get is an automated response telling me the number I dialed isn’t found to be in service. I then try to find someone to contact (is it just me that has a little trouble finding amazon’s CSR information on this site?) after going through a couple of page levels I find the necessary steps that are needed to have someone directly contact me. I enter my phone number so someone can call me. I have a tendency to ramble on when it comes to writing/typing a complaint but a bit briefer when talking to an actual human being. I get another Seattle WA call, this time I answer it straightaway. The person on the other line named “Jeena” sounds friendly enough, but I get a quickly growing suspicion she has an amazon CSR help manual/script along with an Hindi-to-English dictionary in front of her as she is speaking to me. I explain to her everything that had transpired thus far. She expresses her concern but does little to alleviate them or to ameliorate my current situation. Through several distractions on the other end I can barely make heads or tails on what Jeena is trying to convey to me and need to ask several times for clarification. What I gathered from the conversation was the following, that I should see my account updated with the $600 within 12hrs. She also suggested that I try loading an additional smaller amount, like $100 to my account to se if it goes through. I explained that I didn’t feel comfortable sending more currency over into my account when I had the amount that I already sent having not yet gone through. She more or less shared my concerns, but whether or not she was just being sincere or simply parroting is anyone’s guess. I’m going for the latter. Anyway the conversation lasted longer than I would have liked, ended with me getting her name and a promise to have her call me back. That has yet to happen, I’m afraid that my amazon CSR like basically every lady I’ve met has stood me up, lol. So as of 3/12/2019 I haven’t had any updates, with the minor exception of an email from Jeena promising to call me to follow up on seeing whether or not my account reflects the necessary changes. This has been and still is being an aggravating experience. Their is nothing that I could find in the riveting-edge-of-your-seat-easy-to-follow-totally-not-a-boilerplated-lopsided read of their ToS or policies regarding the limit or ammount you could transfer before they get suspicious. I see no reason why, my credit card that I have saved on my own account for quick transactions should have amazon not allowing this to go through. UPDATE: while in the middle of writing this review Jeena called me back. Nothing has yet to be resolved. With a frustrating mixture of trying to calmly as possible voice my frustration while at the same time knowing just how frustrated this has made me I went through basically the same talk I had about 24hrs ago. She explained to me for security reasons that I needed to be verified, though explains nothing of what such a process entails. After explaining to her for the umptieth time that verification isn’t an issue of some arbitrary allotted amount of time but simply of verification I am all but exhausted in this endeavor. I half-jokingly explained after she explained to me Amazon’s reasoning behind this. In the past people hacked into other people accounts to I guess upload gift card amounts then claim said amount was stolen or sent to the wrong account. So basically what I said was “Let me try to understand this. What you’re telling me Jeena is that amazon sees that I sent a $600 amazon gift card using my credit card to my own account, an account I’ve had with the same email address since 2011, and wants to know that I’m actually ‘me’ and not simply pretending to be ‘me’? And in order to verify ‘me’ from ‘me’ some arbitrary amount of time needs to be allotted that somehow gives them the correct answer to my alleged self-identity theft?” Confused? I sure am! Amazon needs to update their policies by giving them crystal clear clarity on the amount you can transfer before they get suspicious. Also the point is ultimately moot, since as I explained to Jeena I could have uploaded the entire amount in increments within 2hrs without amazon freezing my account. Suspiciously high amount of transactions in their (Amazon’s) mind should be no different than smaller ones when it comes to fraudulence. It should be the onus of the customer to contact amazon regarding fraudulent or suspicious activity regarding their own accounts. We should have enough agency & responsibility when it comes to managing our own accounts. I don’t need amazon not telling me how much I can spend, then telling me the amount I transacted using my own card for my own account has enter the level of possible fraudulence. As if there is some actual capstone or touchstone when it comes to when a transaction becomes suspicious or suspected of fraudulence! This has been so far a highly disappointing ordeal:(

text: I have always had great luck with Amazon gift cards via email, so I assumed a physical gift card would be just as great. I was wrong. I ordered this gift card as a Christmas present for my sister. I purchased it on Amazon.com and had it shipped directly to her. Next day shipping was perfect given that I waited until the last minute to do Christmas shopping, but that's where the good part of this card ended. When my sister tried to enter the claim code on the card, she got an error message saying there was something wrong with the claim code. She emailed customer service and the response she got was that she needed to have the sender (me) contact the store I bought the card from to have it activated. Let me remind you that I purchased this card on Amazon.com. So I got in touch with customer service via the online chat option and was told that my issue would have to be elevated to the gift card team and that the card could be activated in 24 to 48 hours. I told the customer service rep that this was not an acceptable option. Then the customer service rep said he'd see what he could do... and came back with the response that I need to go to the store I bought the card from and have make sure the store activates it. Let me remind you yet again that I bought this card from Amazon.com. Then I gave the customer service rep the card's claim code and the Amazon.com order number. The next response I got was that the gift card's claim code did not match up with what was listed for the order number. Ugh. At this point the customer service rep suggested handing this off to the gift card team, which I agreed to. A few hours later I got an email saying that my credit card would be refunded for this purchase. I never asked for a refund... just wanted to get the gift card working, but in a round about way it did solve my problem because I then went ahead and bought an email gift certificate and that worked perfectly. After this experience with the card not working and the repeated suggestion from customer service to go to the store I purchased the card from and have them activate it, when I did in fact buy it on Amazon.com, I would definitely steer away from the physical gift card and go for the email version instead.
